purpose:
A single-user macOS dictation application. It captures speech, recognizes it, optionally rewrites it under a user-selected mode, and inserts the result into the application the user was working in. Every speech and language operation runs on the user's Mac. There is no cloud fallback, no account, no subscription gate, and no artificial cap on recording length or usage; the limits are the hardware and the models the user installs.

In scope: recording controls, text delivery, recording display, built-in modes, custom modes, automatic mode selection, vocabulary, context, languages, input sources, meetings, history, models, desktop behavior. Out of scope: cloud inference, account-based settings synchronization, paywalls, enterprise billing and authentication, and any Windows or iOS client.

The whole product is designed before implementation work is cut, because several requirements constrain the persistence schema, the process model and the ingest boundary in ways that are expensive to retrofit: re-recognizing old audio through a different speech model while keeping every derived artifact attributable (D-029), generating meeting notes from a transcript plus a diarization result plus an editable speaker assignment (D-037), deleting a recording while a worker is producing a result for it (D-024, D-033), snapshotting settings so a later edit cannot change the meaning of a saved result (D-006), recovering a crash at any stage without duplicating delivered text (D-010, D-031), and bounding memory on a multi-hour import across a process boundary (D-018). Left to whichever implementation task first encounters them, those force the schema and the job model into a shape that cannot express them.

This revision settles the items the last review found unresolved. Delivery fallthrough is now rung-specific: only an accessibility error that precedes any effect, or a target-specific rejection signal recorded in a delivery profile, permits the next rung, and the target is revalidated before every posted event and before submission (D-009, D-008, D-010). Notes are their own run created after the diarization result and the first assignment revision commit, and dependencies are recorded in a table that can name a non-result entity (D-037, D-029). Question protection no longer depends on a check the run does not have: when the language-dependent set is unavailable, a mode declaring that it does not answer questions delivers the normalized transcript and holds the rewrite one click away, and no per-mode override changes that (D-012). Every context source is distilled to a term list by default, and any prose path carries a stated disposition (D-012, D-016). There is no unsandboxed inference fallback; the no-egress boundary is a constraint, and F2 chooses the model-access mechanism inside it (D-003, D-028). Capture finalization has an idempotent commit record and a recovery order that incorporates surviving chunks before the packet table is written (D-030). Scheduling now admits non-model ingest work, bounds concurrent sessions, reserves the speech slot for interactive runs so the preview ladder always has a rung, and states a sealer backlog bound with a shedding sequence (D-004, D-011, D-027). Model identity covers every behavior-affecting asset and runs pin the runtime and adapter revision (D-022). Retained context has an owner, a schema and deletion rules (D-039, D-016). Automatic media pausing happens only through an adapter that addresses an identified player; the unattributed media key is now a user action, because a toggle can start a paused player (D-025). Gate ranges carry their basis and approval status, and F1 includes a measurement-only comparison harness so its retention criterion is executable (D-034, D-035, D-020).

Where a claim cannot be made, the design says so instead of weakening the feature. Lexical and structural checks on generated text are necessary conditions, not proof of fidelity. Speaker attribution keeps absent evidence as unknown and keeps manual assignment available (D-023). Every measurement that would evaluate a runtime choice is named, given a range and an action on failure, and marked unperformed.

The historical feature inventories from the mcwhisper and super experiments are evidence about desired scope. Their generated plans and dependency choices do not bind this design.
architecture:
## Layering rule

One rule governs dependency direction. DictationCore depends only on DictationPorts; adapters depend on DictationPorts and on system frameworks; nothing depends on an adapter except the composition root in the app shell. DictationCore contains no AppKit, no AVFoundation, no SQLite and no XPC code, so the run state machine, mode resolution, the vocabulary pipeline, prompt assembly, output checking, delivery policy and scheduling policy can be exercised without a microphone, a model or a window server.

## Package and target layout (D-002)

A Swift Package Manager package, LocalDictation, with library targets:

- DictationPorts: protocols and value types shared by core and adapters (AudioSource, AudioFrame, SpeechRecognizer, TextGenerator, Diarizer, DecoderProvider, TextInserter, FocusObserver, ContextProvider, ModelStore, RecordingStore, LeaseBroker, ShortcutRegistrar, MediaPlayerAdapter, RuntimeCapabilityDescriptor).
- DictationCore: run state machine, RunManifest assembly, mode resolution, vocabulary pipeline, prompt assembly, ResourceScheduler policy, delivery policy.
- TextValidation: transformation contracts, the language-independent check set, per-language validator packs covering segmentation, interrogative detection and content-word extraction.
- DictationStore: SQLite schema, migrations, repositories, the audio chunk journal and its sealer, tombstones, generations, the lease broker, retained-context artifacts.
- AudioIngest: AVAudioEngine microphone source, ScreenCaptureKit system-audio source, AVAssetReader seekable file source, converters to the canonical recognition format.
- SpeechRuntimeWhisperKit, with SpeechRuntimeWhisperCpp built when Intel coverage is required or when F1 rules the default out (D-020); DiarizerSpeakerKit (D-023); LanguageRuntimeLlamaCpp (D-021). Each publishes a RuntimeCapabilityDescriptor carrying its own revision.
- InferenceIPC: message types and the connection client shared by the app and the services.
- SystemIntegration: accessibility insertion and readback, pasteboard, CGEventTap shortcuts, player adapters, status item, permission probes.
- DictationUI: SwiftUI views, recording panel, settings, history browser.

Five bundled XPC services. Four carry code that must not reach the network: SpeechService, GenerationService, DiarizationService and DecodeService. The fifth, ModelDownloader, is the only one that may. Each service is a thin main over a library target, so swift test covers its logic. The Xcode app target produces the bundles and owns entitlements, hardened runtime, privacy usage strings and notarization, none of which is expressible in Package.swift.

## Process model (D-003, D-028, D-036)

The app shell runs unsandboxed, because setting selected text in other applications and running a session-level event tap are unavailable to a sandboxed application outside the Mac App Store; D-036 records the distribution decision that makes this available. Each inference service is sandboxed on its own and its entitlement set omits com.apple.security.network.client, so an outbound connection is denied by the system whatever the linked code contains. That boundary is a constraint of the design and has no fallback outside it.

Model weights reach a service by one of three mechanisms, in preference order: opened file descriptors passed over the connection; a read-only sandbox path exception scoped to Models/blobs for a runtime that insists on opening a model directory by path; materialization by the service of the passed descriptors into its own container, which needs no exception at all and costs a second copy of the weights. F2 decides which mechanism each runtime needs. If a runtime cannot load under any of the three, it is not used for that model kind and the alternative adapter behind the same port is built; a model kind with no adapter that can load inside the boundary is a product-owner escalation rather than a quiet relaxation of the boundary.

Diarization has its own service rather than sharing SpeechService. RESEARCH records that this runtime's default initialization may download models, so it is the component whose acquisition control most needs an enforced boundary, and it loads a different model set whose residency is counted separately (D-027).

Nothing listens on a TCP port. A local HTTP endpoint would bind a port every process on the machine can reach, would need its own authentication, and is the component most likely to acquire forwarding behavior through configuration the app does not own; RESEARCH raises that for llama.cpp's server tooling.

ModelDownloader holds the network entitlement, an allowlist of model hosts, and write access confined to Models/.staging. It runs only on explicit user action, and no inference service can start it.

A service can fail or be terminated independently of its client, so connection interruption is a first-class event. The run fails at its current stage, committed results stand, and the next admission loads the model into a fresh service. A service holds only state the app can rebuild from the run manifest and the store: its loaded models, the current job's window queue, that job's decoder state, and the current prompt, none of which it writes to disk.

## Processing runs and stages (D-029, D-037)

A recording owns audio artifacts. Every piece of derived text belongs to a processing_run, which pins the settings and inputs that produced it and names its entry stage. Run kinds: dictation (capture through delivery), import, meeting (two-stream capture through diarization), notes, reprocess_recognition, reprocess_diarization, reprocess_text.

The stage set is idle, arming, capturing, sealing, recognizing, diarizing, refining, rewriting, noting, delivering, terminal. A run enters at the stage its kind declares and visits only the stages its kind declares. Every stage a run can occupy has a cancellation effect (D-007) and a recovery transition (D-031).

A notes run is a separate run rather than a tail stage of the meeting run, because its manifest must pin the diarization result and the assignment revision, and those do not exist when a meeting run arms. When a meeting run's diarization result commits, the store also commits assignment revision 1 derived from the clusters, and the app creates a notes run whose manifest names the transcript result, the diarization result, the assignment revision, the identity-name set hash, the mode revision and the generation model installation. Regeneration after a rename or a re-diarization creates another notes run the same way.

## The lifetime of a dictation run (D-006)

Component boundaries follow this sequence.

1. idle.
2. arming. The microphone stream starts immediately on the trigger and its frames go into a pre-roll ring, so the first word is not lost while the rest of arming runs concurrently: resolve the effective mode from the automatic-selection rules (D-014); resolve the delivery target, meaning frontmost process id, bundle identifier, window number, focused accessibility element and that element's readback capability (D-008); sample context sources in parallel against a 200 ms budget (D-016); assemble a RunManifest naming mode revision, model installations, runtime and adapter revisions, vocabulary revision, language setting, translation flag and validator pack set; allocate a UUIDv7 recording id and run id; create the session directory; write and fsync manifest v0 with disposition=active.
3. capturing. The pre-roll ring is flushed into the chunk journal ahead of the live frames (D-030); the writer appends timestamped native frames; the provisional recognizer consumes a parallel tap; the panel shows live text and an envelope (D-011).
4. sealing. Stop the source, drain the sealer backlog, write and commit the finalized artifact (D-030), then commit the recording row, artifact row and run row in one transaction. That is the first point at which the recording exists in History; ownership before it is the session directory (D-033).
5. recognizing. One pass over the complete audio produces a recognition result with segment timings and per-segment average log-probability. The provisional stream is discarded instead of promoted; it was computed over partial context and is a different artifact.
6. refining. Deterministic vocabulary replacement and optional filler removal produce a normalized result derived from that recognition result (D-015).
7. rewriting, only when the mode has a generation stage: prompt assembly, generation in the service, contract checking (D-012).
8. delivering. One ladder attempt sequence with per-rung records, guarded by a committed idempotency record (D-010).
9. terminal: complete, cancelled(stage), failed(stage, reason), or delivery_unresolved.

Imports enter at capturing with a seekable source and no delivery target. Meetings enter at arming with two sources, no delivery target, and run through diarizing. Reprocessing enters at recognizing, diarizing, refining or rewriting with a manifest naming its parent inputs. One machine serves every input source and every reprocessing path, which is why cancellation, recovery and deletion each have a single definition.

## Concurrency, lanes and admission (D-004)

One RunActor per processing run owns that run's state, rows and files, and is the only writer for them. Two runs on the same recording are serialized by the recording's lease (D-033). The audio callback thread never touches an actor, allocates or locks; it writes frames and a 10 ms RMS and peak envelope into two lock-free rings.

A single ResourceScheduler actor admits work of both kinds.

Non-model work is admitted by session count, not by memory slot. At most one live capture session runs at a time; a meeting is one session with two streams, and a second trigger while one is active is refused with a message rather than queued. Live capture writing and incremental sealing are exempt from admission and run on a capture lane above batch quality of service, because a live source cannot be deferred without losing data. Seekable ingest is not exempt: an import's decoding, conversion, journaling and sealing occupy one of a bounded number of ingest slots, one by default and configurable to two. With those bounds and the credit windows of D-018, non-model resident memory is bounded and counted in the budget of D-027.

Model-bound work is admitted by slot and by summed footprint. Slots are speech-primary, speech-preview, generation and diarization, at most one occupant each (D-027). From arming until its recognition result commits, an interactive dictation run holds a reservation on the speech-primary slot: any batch speech job is preempted at admission time, which is why the preview ladder in D-011 always has a rung available rather than waiting behind a long import. Preemption yields and resumes only where the runtime's descriptor records verified checkpoint equivalence; otherwise the batch job restarts from the beginning when it is re-admitted, which is correct without that evidence. A user setting can defer preemption until the batch job finishes, at the cost of delaying the dictation, and the panel says which policy is in force.

The sealer has a backlog bound rather than a quality-of-service promise. If the unsealed journal backlog for any live stream exceeds 30 seconds of audio for more than 10 seconds, batch admission pauses; above 60 seconds, ingest slots are released and imports stop; above 120 seconds, capture stops and the recording is sealed as interrupted with the reason recorded. That bound is what makes cancel-during-sealing latency bounded, and F3 measures it under CPU and disk contention.

## Component responsibilities

- ModeResolver (core): a pure function from foreground application, URL when readable, explicit override and the ordered rule list to a mode revision.
- VocabularyPipeline (core): pure text-to-text with an explicit stage order, an explicit match precedence and ICU-based segmentation.
- ContextDistiller (core): reduces a sampled source to a capped term list, or passes prose when the mode opts in, recording which form was used per source.
- PromptAssembler (core): mode instructions, then context in the form D-016 allows for its source, fenced with a per-run random delimiter and labeled as reference material, then the normalized transcript, then the task line restated.
- ContractChecker (TextValidation): runs the language-independent set always and the language-dependent set when a pack exists, and reports which checks ran; disposition is decided in core by D-012.
- DeliveryCoordinator (core policy) with TextInserter (adapter): target resolution, revalidation, per-rung fallthrough rules and the confirmation predicate live in policy; only the mechanism lives in the adapter, so the whole ladder is testable without a window server.
- RecordingStore with LeaseBroker (DictationStore): the only writers of History rows, library files and retained-context artifacts, and the enforcement point for tombstones, generations and leases for every writer including retention.
- InferenceClient (InferenceIPC): connection lifecycle, credit accounting, interruption handling, per-service residency accounting.

## Why this supports the whole scope as capabilities land

The run state machine, the manifest snapshot, the provenance graph, the recovery table and the lease protocol are built first against fake adapters. Every later capability adds an adapter behind an existing port, a result kind, or a validator language pack. None of them changes how a run is recorded, cancelled, recovered or deleted. The parts that are expensive to change late are exercised against fakes, where cancel-at-every-stage and kill-at-every-boundary suites are cheap to run.
data_lifecycle:
## Stores and ownership

DictationStore owns everything under ~/Library/Application Support/LocalDictation/:

```
library.sqlite                                  metadata, runs, results, FTS index (WAL)
Recordings/<uuid>/manifest.json                 fsynced at run start, carries disposition
Recordings/<uuid>/journal/<stream>/<seq>.pcm    durable capture chunks
Recordings/<uuid>/journal/<stream>/index.log    packet index and seal record
Recordings/<uuid>/audio/<stream>.caf            sealed library artifact
Recordings/<uuid>/source/<original filename>    imported original
Recordings/<uuid>/context/<sampleId>.txt        retained context text, when opted in
Models/blobs/<setHash>/                         immutable verified installs
Models/notices/<setHash>/                       retained licences and notices
Models/.staging/<uuid>/                         in-flight downloads and imports
Scratch/<jobId>/                                service temporaries
```

One writer connection in WAL mode; readers use separate connections. RunActor never writes SQLite directly. It calls repository methods that enforce tombstone, generation and lease rules. Notices live outside Models/blobs so that archiving an installation, which deletes the blob directory, cannot delete the notices it claims to retain (D-038).

## Ownership before the History row exists (D-033)

A lease requires a recording row, and capture creates that row only at the sealing commit. Between arming and that commit the unit of ownership is the session directory: its path contains a UUIDv7 no other actor can name, the owning RunActor is its only writer, and manifest.json carries a disposition field, fsynced on change, with values active, cancelled and abandoned. Cancellation or deletion requested before the commit is recorded by writing the disposition, not by a tombstone row. Recovery treats a session directory with no committed recording row according to its manifest disposition. The lease protocol begins at the commit and covers everything afterwards.

## Provenance graph (D-029, D-037)

- recordings(id, created_at, source_kind, duration_ms, interrupted, deleted_at, generation, audio_state, display_run_id)
- audio_artifacts(id, recording_id, role, path, container, codec, sample_rate, channels, sealed_at, sha256, byte_length), role in {microphone, system, imported_original}
- processing_runs(id, recording_id, recording_generation, kind, entry_stage, manifest_json, runtime_revisions_json, state, started_at, ended_at, reason)
- results(id, run_id, recording_id, kind, primary_input_result_id, text, params_json, params_rendered, created_at), kind in {recognition, normalized, rewritten, translation, diarization, notes}
- result_dependencies(result_id, input_kind, input_id, role), input_kind in {result, speaker_assignment_revision, audio_artifact}, role in {transcript, diarization, assignments, prior_notes, audio}
- segments, speaker_clusters, speaker_identities, speaker_identity_names, speaker_assignment_revisions, speaker_assignments, modes, mode_revisions, vocabulary_revisions, rules, model_installations, model_assets, active_models, leases, context_digests, retained_context, delivery_attempts, delivery_attempt_rungs, delivery_profiles, jobs

Every result names its primary input through a column, which carries the common single-parent chain: normalized derives from recognition, rewritten from normalized, a translation from whichever result the user translated, and a recognition result has NULL and roots its run's chain. Anything a result depends on that is not its primary input, including entities that are not results, is a row in result_dependencies. A notes result has the transcript as primary input and dependency rows for the diarization result and the assignment revision. A diarization result has no textual parent and dependency rows for its audio artifacts. The previous single-column form could not name an assignment revision at all, which is why the link table carries a typed input kind rather than a second result column.

A recording can hold several recognition results and several diarization results, one per run, each carrying the model installation and the runtime and adapter revisions that produced it. Results are immutable after insert, enforced by a trigger that rejects UPDATE on results.text; reprocessing inserts and never replaces. recordings.display_run_id is a user-movable pointer deciding what the list view shows.

## Speaker assignments as revisions (D-037)

A diarization result is immutable and holds cluster boundaries. The mapping from segment to named speaker is separate and versioned: speaker_assignment_revisions(id, recording_id, diarization_result_id, content_hash, created_at) with speaker_assignments(revision_id, segment_id, identity_id, attribution_state). Revision 1 is committed in the same transaction as the diarization result, so an assignment revision always exists before any notes run starts. Every user edit, whether an assignment, a merge or a split, appends a revision. Identity display names are append-only in speaker_identity_names(identity_id, name, effective_from), because a rename must not silently change what an older transcript view showed.

A notes run pins the transcript result id, the diarization result id, the assignment revision id and the identity-name set hash in its manifest, and the first three appear in result_dependencies. Note text is immutable and contains the names in effect at generation, so a later rename or a re-run of diarization cannot change the note's meaning. History compares the pinned identifiers against current state and shows, on a note, that speakers were renamed or re-diarized since it was produced, with a regenerate action that creates a new notes run.

## Persistence choice (D-005)

SQLite through GRDB with FTS5 over result text. History search is a stated requirement and FTS5 with bm25 ranking and snippets is why SQLite wins here; SwiftData and Core Data have no comparable text index and their migration behavior is harder to test against fixtures. Schema versions are numbered migrations, each with a test that runs the migration against a fixture database captured at the prior version. Retained context is not added to the FTS index, so search returns the user's own speech and its derived text rather than the documents that happened to be on screen.

## Audio: journal, sealing, finalization and recovery (D-030)

Capture writes fixed-period chunks, two seconds by default, of raw interleaved Int16 at the source's native rate into journal/<stream>/. Each chunk is written to <seq>.pcm.part, fsynced, renamed to <seq>.pcm, and the directory is fsynced. A chunk carries no header; its format lives in the fsynced manifest, so any complete chunk decodes on its own and a torn final chunk is discardable.

The incremental sealer runs on the capture lane. Its cycle for chunk N is ordered so that the index never names bytes that are not durable:

1. Encode chunk N into ALAC packets.
2. Append the packet bytes to the CAF data chunk in audio/<stream>.caf. The data chunk size field is written as -1 during capture, which CAF defines as extending to end of file, so no header rewrite is needed while recording.
3. fsync the CAF file. Audio bytes are durable before anything refers to them.
4. Append one data record to index.log and fsync it. The record is {magic, kind=data, record_seq, chunk_seq, first_packet_index, packet_count, frames_per_packet, caf_data_byte_offset, caf_data_byte_length, varint packet byte sizes for each of packet_count packets, crc32 over the record}. Per-packet sizes are present because an ALAC packet table cannot be reconstructed from a count and an offset.
5. Delete the journal chunks covered by durable data records, then fsync the journal directory.

Finalization at end of capture is itself crash-safe and repeatable, and its commit point is a record rather than the file's shape:

1. Encode and commit any remaining chunks through the cycle above, so every surviving sample is described by a durable data record before the packet table is written.
2. Append the pakt chunk built from the accepted data records, then fsync.
3. Patch the data chunk size field to its final value, then fsync.
4. Hash the file and append a seal record {magic, kind=seal, last_data_record_seq, pakt_byte_offset, file_length, sha256, crc32}, then fsync.
5. Commit the rows.

Recovery replays index.log from the start, accepting records whose crc32 validates and whose byte ranges lie within the file's actual length; the first record failing either test ends the durable prefix and the rest of the log is discarded, which is how a torn tail is rejected. If the prefix ends in a valid seal record whose file length and hash match the file, the artifact is finalized and recovery stops. Otherwise recovery truncates the CAF file to the end of the last accepted data record, which removes any partially written packet table or size patch, re-encodes and commits any surviving journal chunks through the ordinary cycle, and then runs finalization from step 2. Repeating that sequence after another crash produces the same result, because every step derives from the accepted prefix.

Worst-case loss is the unsealed tail: at most one chunk period plus data the operating system had not yet flushed within it. The exact bound comes from gate F3, which has not been run; the chunk period is the tuning knob if the measurement is worse than expected, and the structural fallback if reconstruction proves invalid at any period is to stop deleting chunks until the finalized artifact has been decoded end to end and hashed, at the cost of journal storage equal to the whole recording.

Canonical recognition format is 16 kHz mono Float32, produced by a converter stage after the ingest port. Sealed dictation audio is 16 kHz mono ALAC at roughly 50 to 60 MB per hour, by arithmetic from 16-bit PCM at 115 MB per hour; meeting streams are sealed at native rate, which is larger and is reported in the library size view. Lossy encoding is rejected because re-recognition with a better model later is a requirement. Imported files are copied in their original encoding and decoded on demand.

## Model installations, identity, states and notices (D-022, D-038)

An installation is identified by publisher, revision string and a SHA-256 over a content-addressed installation manifest that lists the relative path and SHA-256 of every behavior-affecting asset: weights, tokenizer or vocabulary, model configuration, prompt or chat template, feature-extraction parameters, and any companion file the runtime reads. Hashing only the weight files would let a tokenizer or template change output while History reported the same identity. model_installations records that identity, runtime kind, model kind, declared capabilities, install time, origin and lifecycle state in {installed, archived, orphaned_runtime, missing}. model_assets records one row per asset with its own SHA-256, size, license identifier and the path of the retained notice under Models/notices/<setHash>/.

Every run also records the runtime revision, the adapter revision and the capability-descriptor version in processing_runs.runtime_revisions_json, because two results can share an installation identity and still differ if the runtime changed underneath them.

Archiving is what bounds storage when a runtime is replaced (D-038): the installation row, manifest hashes, capabilities and notices are retained so every History result stays attributable, while the weight blobs are released. Results also carry params_rendered, a human-readable snapshot of the parameters written at insert time, so an old row remains readable after its adapter is removed from the build.

## Settings snapshots and derived results

A mode is a named entity with an append-only chain of mode_revisions, each content-addressed over prompt, formatting rules, transformation contract, context representation settings, validator language list and model selections. A run's manifest stores revision identifiers. Editing a mode creates a revision and leaves saved results pointing at the revision that produced them, which makes the requirement that later edits must not silently change a saved result structural instead of procedural. History shows the producing revision and diffs it against the current one.

## Context: retention, ownership and ephemeral lifetimes (D-016, D-039)

By default the store keeps a SHA-256 digest, byte length, source kind and representation per context sample in context_digests, and not the text. That is enough to tell a user reprocessing an old recording that the original context is unavailable, without retaining copies of unrelated documents and screens.

When a mode opts into retention, the sample is an owned artifact: retained_context(id, run_id, recording_id, source_kind, representation, path, byte_length, sha256, created_at) with the text in Recordings/<uuid>/context/<sampleId>.txt. The row is written in the same transaction as the run's other rows, the file is fsynced before that commit, and both are removed by the same deletion and retention paths as audio, so retained context cannot outlive its recording. Migrations own the table like any other. Protection is the file system's: the library is not separately encrypted, which is the same posture as the audio and transcripts beside it.

Transient copies have stated release points. A captured screen frame lives only inside the arming task, is passed to Vision in memory and is released when text extraction returns; it is never written to disk. Source strings from accessibility and the pasteboard are released once the prompt is assembled, and the assembled prompt itself lives in the RunActor until the generation reply completes, fails or is cancelled, and in the service in the job's arena, freed at job end by the same three paths and destroyed with the process if the service crashes. XPC message buffers are released as credit is returned per window. Generation key-value state is freed at job end or at model unload. Scratch/<jobId> is removed when the job ends and swept at launch. No inference service writes prompts, context or transcripts to disk; DecodeService writes decoded audio windows into its job scratch and nothing else.

## Interrupted operations (D-031)

The ordering rule is stated once: an externally visible irreversible effect is preceded by a durable record of intent, which is what delivery does, while a local idempotent effect is followed by its commit, which is what sealing does. Recovery at launch reconciles manifests, files and rows by run state.

- arming: remove the session directory. No rows.
- capturing: seal the journal through the finalization sequence, commit the recording with interrupted set, mark the run cancelled(capturing, crash). Nothing was delivered; History offers recognition.
- sealing: a finalized or partially finalized artifact may exist without rows. Recovery is the idempotent sequence above, after which it commits as for capturing, or applies the manifest disposition if that disposition is cancelled.
- recognizing: no partial transcript is saved; the run becomes failed(recognizing, interrupted); audio is retained; History offers a new recognition run.
- diarizing: no partial diarization is saved; the run becomes failed(diarizing, interrupted); the recognition result and audio stand; History offers a new diarization run.
- refining: the recognition result is committed and immutable, and refining is a pure function of committed inputs pinned in the manifest, so recovery re-runs it, commits the normalized result and stops.
- rewriting: the run becomes failed(rewriting, interrupted); the normalized result stands; History offers a rewrite run. Recovery never resumes generation.
- noting: the run becomes failed(noting, interrupted); the transcript, diarization result and assignment revision stand; History offers a new notes run.
- meeting completed with no notes run: recovery does not start one, because that would consume a model without user action; History shows notes not generated with a Generate action.
- delivering: any delivery_attempts row in pending, in_progress or unconfirmed becomes needs_review, the run becomes delivery_unresolved, and nothing is re-posted (D-010).
- Scratch directories, staged model directories and model blobs with no installed row and no live lease are removed. Leases whose holder process is gone are reclaimed (D-033).

## Deletion during active processing (D-024, D-033)

Deletion sets recordings.deleted_at, increments recordings.generation, and signals cancellation to every lease holder. Each worker carries recording id and generation from admission. A worker's commit is one transaction that re-reads the recording row and aborts if the row is missing, tombstoned or at a different generation; on abort it removes its scratch directory and returns. The existence check and the insert cannot be separated, so a late response cannot recreate a deleted recording, and the generation counter covers delete-then-recreate at the same identifier. Deleting a recording that has not yet committed is the pre-commit disposition path.

Hard deletion of rows, artifacts, retained context and FTS entries runs when the last lease on the recording is released, and again at launch. Until then the recording is hidden and reported as deleting instead of as reclaimed space.

## Retention (D-033)

Retention defaults to keeping everything. Optional age-based, size-based and audio-discarding policies are ordinary deletion jobs: they acquire the same leases, observe the same generation checks, and skip any recording with a live lease held by a worker, a player or an export, retrying on the next pass. Discarding audio moves recordings.audio_state to audio_discarded, which History displays; playback, re-recognition and re-diarization are then unavailable while text reprocessing remains available. The first run of any policy lists exactly what it would remove before removing it.

## Cancellation by run stage (D-007)

Cancellation has a defined effect at every stage a run can occupy, and the panel names that effect when it happens. Cancelling one run never alters results committed by another run.

- arming: nothing kept; the pre-roll ring and session directory are discarded; no rows.
- capturing: capture stops; the journal is discarded by default and no History row is created; a per-mode setting seals it as an interrupted recording instead.
- sealing: the seal runs to completion, because it is bounded, idempotent and needed for any disposition to be coherent. The wait is bounded by the sealer backlog rule in D-004, which caps the unsealed backlog at 30 seconds of audio under normal operation and stops capture rather than letting it grow past 120 seconds. The run then applies the capture-stage disposition: by default the artifact and session directory are removed and no row is committed; under the per-mode setting the recording commits marked interrupted. No later stage is entered.
- recognizing: the worker stops at its next checkpoint; audio is kept; no partial transcript is saved, because a truncated transcript that looks complete is worse than none.
- diarizing: the worker stops; the recognition result and audio are kept; no partial diarization is saved, because a segment set covering part of a meeting would be indistinguishable in the transcript view from one covering all of it.
- refining: the recognition result stands; the normalized result is dropped.
- rewriting: generation stops; the normalized result is kept and offered for delivery.
- noting: generation stops; the transcript, diarization result and assignment revision stand; no partial notes are saved.
- delivering: cancellable until the first rung's external effect begins. After that the app records which rung began, reports that delivery was attempted, and stops; it does not try to undo an edit in another application.

## Permissions as a capability matrix (D-032)

Revocation is handled per capability and per run state in place of one global rule. Losing a capability terminates only the work that capability serves.

- Microphone denied at launch: recording controls disabled with a link to the settings pane; file import still works. Revoked during capturing: capture stops, the journal is sealed, the recording is marked interrupted, nothing is delivered.
- Screen Recording denied: system audio and screen context unavailable; microphone recording, all modes, and rules that do not need screen context continue; meetings degrade to microphone only with a visible marker. Revoked during capturing of a meeting: the system stream ends and is marked truncated at a timestamp, the microphone stream continues, and the recording states which streams cover which interval.
- Accessibility denied or revoked: selected-text insertion, readback and target revalidation are unavailable, so delivery holds the result rather than posting events into a target it cannot identify; recognition, diarization and rewriting continue to completion.
- Input Monitoring denied or revoked: the event tap cannot run, so push-to-talk is unavailable and toggle falls back to a Carbon hotkey; an in-flight run continues and the panel gains a stop control.
- Automation for a browser denied: URL predicates do not match, rule evaluation continues, and the panel shows that the mode came from the fallback. Automation for a media player denied: that player's adapter is unavailable, so D-025's owned-pause path is unavailable for it.
- Restoration: capabilities are re-probed on the relevant system notification and at each arming, and the panel reports a recovered capability once instead of on every session.

## Secure input

If IsSecureEventInputEnabled() is true at arming, the run records but is marked delivery-unavailable up front. If it becomes true by delivery time, the app posts no events, holds the result in History, offers copy, and states that another application has secure input active. Password fields are the common case, and silently dropping text there would be the worst available failure.

## Delivery: target, revalidation, rung rules and attempt states (D-008, D-009, D-010)

Exactly one delivery target is resolved for each focus outcome:

- The latched element is still focused: the target is the latched element.
- The latched application is frontmost with a different element focused, and the per-mode follow-focus setting is on, which is the default: the target is the currently focused element, resolved at delivery.
- Same application, follow-focus off: no target; hold.
- A different application is frontmost, or the latched application quit: no target; hold, with a card offering Deliver and Copy. Re-activating the latched application first is opt-in, because it steals focus.

Resolving the target once is not enough, because Command-V, synthesized typing and the submit Return reach whatever is focused when each event is posted. The coordinator therefore revalidates immediately before every event-based rung and before the Return: the frontmost process, window number and focused element must still equal the resolved target. Any mismatch ends the attempt as unconfirmed, with no retry, no further rung and no submission.

Confirmation is a predicate over content, not over length. Before the operation the coordinator records the target's selected range and, where readable, its value around the insertion point. After the operation it re-reads and confirms that the expected text appears at the expected insertion location with the caret or selection immediately after it.

Fallthrough is rung-specific, because the rungs differ in what they can prove:

- Rung 1 sets AXSelectedText on the target. AXValue is never set, because RESEARCH records that setting an editable field's value can replace its contents. A non-success AXError returned by the accessibility call is an explicit negative and permits rung 2, because that result is returned before any effect on the target. If the call succeeds, the predicate decides: confirmed, or unconfirmed when the predicate cannot be evaluated. A successful call with an unreadable target does not fall through.
- Rung 2 writes the pasteboard and posts Command-V. An unchanged readback is not an explicit negative here. Posting the event carries no acknowledgment of consumption, and a delayed consumer can apply the paste after the readback, so treating an unchanged value as rejection is exactly how a paragraph gets typed on top of a paste that later lands. Rung 2 falls through to rung 3 only when the target's delivery profile records a target-specific rejection signal and that signal fires. Every other outcome is confirmed by the predicate or unconfirmed.
- Rung 3 synthesizes Unicode typing, capped at 400 characters; above the cap the app holds and offers copy.

Attempt states and transitions (D-010): pending is committed before any event is posted or any accessibility write is issued; in_progress while a rung is running; delivered on a confirmed predicate; rejected when a rung returns its own explicit negative, which is not terminal and hands off to the next rung; unconfirmed when the predicate is not evaluable, when revalidation fails, or when a rung ends with neither confirmation nor its own negative, which is terminal for the automatic path; held when no target exists or the cap is exceeded; failed on an error before any effect. Terminal states are delivered, unconfirmed, held, failed and needs_review. delivery_attempt_rungs records, per rung, whether its external effect began, what signal was observed and the outcome, so recovery and the interface can say what was attempted. At launch, pending, in_progress and unconfirmed become needs_review; delivered, held and failed are left as they are, so a successful past delivery is never re-surfaced. Nothing is ever re-posted automatically.

Pasteboard handling: snapshot before writing, and restore only after a confirmed delivery while changeCount still equals ours, or on the user's explicit Restore clipboard action. There is no timer-based restore, because a delayed consumer can read the pasteboard after any interval the app could pick. After an unconfirmed outcome the transcript stays on the pasteboard and the panel says so. Where the pasteboard cannot be snapshotted, meaning it exceeds the configured snapshot limit or holds promised files or unsupported types, the user is told before anything is written and chooses between proceeding without restore and copy-only.

Submission: the Return is posted after a confirmed delivery, to a revalidated target, when the submit modifier was held at stop, whichever rung achieved the delivery. A held, rejected or unconfirmed attempt never auto-submits.

## Service failures (D-003)

A service crash or termination invalidates the connection. The client marks the run failed at its current stage with the exit status, keeps every committed result, releases the job's credit and slot, and offers retry. Three crashes on one model installation mark it suspect in the model list. Because a service holds only loaded models, the current job's window queue and its prompt, retry reloads from the manifest and needs no state salvage. A service that stops consuming credit is treated as hung after a no-progress interval measured against delivered windows, and is terminated by the client.

## Model and runtime failures (D-022, D-038)

- Download interrupted or hash mismatch against the installation manifest: the staging directory is removed, no blob is created, the active installation is untouched, and the error names expected and computed digests.
- User-supplied model failing its per-kind load smoke test: it stays in staging with the error attached and nothing is activated. The smoke test checks that the runtime can load the assets and produce output on a fixed sample; it is a capability check and never a quality judgment, so a compatible model with no benchmark row activates normally and is labeled unmeasured.
- Model assets missing for a pinned run: if the installation is archived, the run is refused up front with an offer to restore the assets by import or download; if the installation claims installed but assets are gone, the row moves to missing and the same offer appears. Loading never falls back to downloading.
- Runtime or adapter revision no longer present for a reprocess that pinned it: the run is refused with the recorded revision named, and the user can run with the current revision as a new run rather than as a reproduction.
- Pairing exceeding the residency budget: refused at activation with the arithmetic shown, the refusal stating whether the numbers are measured or declared, and the user can override, because it is their machine.

## Resource and storage failures

- Sealer backlog growth: the shed sequence in D-004 pauses batch admission, then stops import ingest, then stops capture and seals as interrupted, each step reported in the panel with the backlog figure.
- Disk full during capture: capture stops, the journal is sealed to the last complete chunk, the recording is marked interrupted, and the panel reports the reason.
- Journal fsync failing repeatedly: capture stops instead of continuing with an unrecoverable tail.
- Unsupported import format: the source is untouched, the session directory is removed, and the error names the format and the optional external decoder path (D-018, D-028).
- Audio device removed mid-run: capture stops and the recording is sealed as interrupted. The app does not silently switch devices under an active recording.
- A second recording trigger while a live capture session is active: refused with a message naming the active session, rather than queued behind it.

## Generated text whose compliance cannot be established (D-012)

Checks are divided by what they need. The language-independent set runs on every generation: expansion ratio against the mode's limit, context overlap rejecting any span of eight or more tokens present in the context block and absent from the transcript, vocabulary term survival, script sanity, and orthographic interrogative-marker detection over the transcript, which finds question marks in the scripts the run uses and cannot find a question asked without one. The language-dependent set needs a validator pack: interrogative survival in order under proper sentence segmentation, content-word recall, and detection of sentences with no content-word support in the input.

An observed violation in either set is a contract violation: the run retries once with a stricter instruction, and on a second violation the delivered text is the normalized transcript, the generated text is retained as a result marked contract_violation, and the panel says which check failed. A sentence with no content-word support is a violation on the same path; for a mode whose contract declares summarization, the citation requirement governs instead and uncited bullets are dropped.

When the run's language has no pack, the language-dependent checks are unavailable rather than failed. The model still runs, and its output is produced, retained, searchable and one click from delivery, because pack coverage must not restrict which models a user may run. What changes is the automatic path: for a mode whose contract declares answersQuestions false, an unavailable question-preservation check means the delivered text is the normalized transcript, whatever the orthographic marker check reports. That check can find a question mark; it cannot establish that no question was asked, so making delivery depend on it would put the protection back on a detector the run does not have. There is no per-mode override, because an override would let a mode declaring that it does not answer questions deliver unchecked rewrites, and the specification's condition is that answering must be explicitly part of the selected mode. A mode intended for a language with no pack can be authored as a revision that declares answersQuestions true, which the mode indicator shows.

Context representation carries its own disposition. All three sources are distilled to a capped term list by default, including focused-element text, which removes instruction-shaped sentences from the prompt rather than detecting them afterwards. A mode may opt into prose per source. When any source contributed prose, automatic delivery of generated text additionally requires the language-dependent set to be available and to pass; otherwise the normalized transcript is delivered and the generated text is held one click away. Prose participation is recorded on the result and shown in the panel and History.

The claim stops there. These checks are necessary conditions. They can pass on text whose meaning changed, and on the prose path an instruction followed in words that do not appear in the context is not detectable by any check listed here. The bounds on the damage are that the transcript is always preserved, that delivery is the only automatic external effect and is reviewable, and that the adversarial corpus in verification is the standing test of how far the checks reach.

## Meeting attribution with weak evidence (D-023)

The diarizer supplies cluster boundaries. RESEARCH establishes that its result type exposes speaker centroid embeddings with cosine-distance helpers, that a speaker may have no centroid, and that the declaration does not establish per-segment confidence or margin outputs. The schema follows that exactly: per-segment calibrated confidence is stored as unknown, no per-segment margin is stored, and the only quantitative evidence retained is centroid cosine distance where a centroid exists. Every segment carries attribution_state in {assigned, unverified, assigned_by_user, unattributed}; without per-segment evidence the default is unverified. The transcript shows the cluster label with an unverified marker, and notes attribute only segments whose state is assigned_by_user or assigned. Cross-recording identity is proposed only where both sides have centroids, is always presented for confirmation rather than applied, and is unavailable for a speaker with no centroid, where naming stays per-recording. Segments whose microphone content correlates with delayed system audio are marked probable echo and excluded from microphone-side attribution. A user can assign, merge or split speakers at any time; each edit appends an assignment revision (D-037) and sets attribution_state to assigned_by_user, which no later diarization run overwrites.

## Desktop restore failures (D-025)

Automatic pausing and automatic resumption both require an adapter that addresses an identified player: the adapter queries the player's state, issues a one-way pause command to that player, observes the transition to paused, and records ownership of that specific pause. Only an owned pause is resumed automatically, and only while the player still reports paused and no other client has changed it.

For a player with no adapter the app takes no automatic action. The panel and menu offer Pause media as an explicit user action, which posts the play-pause key and is labeled as a toggle whose recipient and effect the app cannot confirm; the same surface offers Resume playback afterwards. The earlier design posted that key automatically whenever the default output device reported a running client, and that is unsafe in a case REVIEW_NOTES names: a paused player can receive the toggle while an unrelated client keeps the device active, which starts playback. Input device volume is restored only if the current value still equals the value the app set; any mismatch means no restore and a note that the setting was left as found.

## What this section covers

Task-level phases are produced after design acceptance. What belongs here is the ordering the design imposes, the evidence that closes each capability area, and the cost of the extensions the specification asks about. Every ordering constraint exists because a later decision depends on an earlier result, and every acceptance item names evidence in place of a completion claim.

## Evidence gates that precede frozen boundaries (D-034)

Five measurements can invalidate a boundary, so each runs before the boundary it could overturn. Each gate's range, its basis and its failure action are recorded in verification and approved under D-035 before the gate runs. They govern shipped defaults; none of them gates a compatible model a user imports.

- F1, runtime harness. Two arms, because a comparison needs both sides to exist: the shipping WhisperKit adapter and a measurement-only whisper.cpp harness that is not the shipping adapter and does not carry its integration work. Measures word error rate on a fixed corpus, time to final transcript, service peak resident size at 10 minutes, 1 hour and 3 hours, cancellation latency at p50 and p95, whether resuming from a window checkpoint reproduces the unpreempted transcript, and the preview arm described under D-011. It precedes freezing the scheduler's preemption policy (D-004), the admission arithmetic of D-027 and the default pairing (D-020).
- F2, service isolation. Load each model kind inside its sandboxed service by all three access mechanisms: descriptor passing, a read-only path exception scoped to Models/blobs, and materialization inside the service's own container. Attempt an outbound connection and assert denial, attempt a write outside the job scratch directory and assert denial, and repeat both from the external decoder the decode service spawns. It precedes freezing the entitlement set and the model-access path (D-003, D-028). It does not decide the boundary, which is fixed.
- F3, capture durability and sealer behavior. Kill the writer at randomized offsets across chunk boundaries, at both per-chunk fsync points and at every finalization write, and kill again during recovery. Record the maximum lost interval, whether the rebuilt packet table decodes end to end, and whether repeated recovery converges. Separately, measure the sealer backlog under CPU and disk contention, including a concurrent import, to check the 30-second bound and the shed sequence. It precedes approving recovery outcomes for capturing and sealing and the cancel-during-sealing bound (D-030, D-031, D-007).
- F4, insertion and pasteboard matrix. Selected-text insertion and paste with the confirmation predicate across the target applications listed under verification, recording whether existing content survives, whether the predicate is evaluable, whether any target-specific rejection signal exists that would justify a rung 3 entry in that target's profile, and when each target reads the pasteboard. It precedes shipping delivery profiles (D-009). The ladder does not wait on it: with no profile entry, rung 3 is unreachable and an unevaluable outcome is unconfirmed.
- F5, diarizer adapter inventory. Against the pinned SpeakerKit version, record which fields DiarizationResult exposes, which speakers receive centroids on two-speaker and four-speaker fixtures, the resident size and wall time of the segmenter and embedder at the configured concurrency, and whether the explicit download flag and model folder suppress acquisition under a network-denied profile. It precedes freezing the meeting schema and the diarization residency numbers (D-023, D-027, D-037).

## Dependency order among capability areas

- The store, the run state machine, the manifest, the lease protocol and the recovery table depend on nothing external and come first, exercised against fake adapters. Everything else depends on them.
- Capture and delivery depend on the run machine, the recovery contract and the capability matrix (D-006, D-031, D-032). Neither depends on a model, so both can be accepted before any runtime is integrated.
- Recognition depends on capture and on the model store, because a run pins an installation and a runtime revision (D-022).
- Vocabulary and the Standard mode depend on recognition. Generation modes depend on vocabulary, on the check sets and packs (D-012) and on F2, which governs how the generation service is launched.
- Automatic mode selection and context depend on modes existing, on the retained-context schema (D-039) and on the permission matrix for their degraded states.
- System audio and file import depend on the ingest port, on ingest admission (D-004) and on the memory slope from F1.
- Meetings depend on system-audio capture, on F5, on the diarization service and on the acquisition path for weights the application does not bundle. Notes depend on the notes run and the assignment-revision schema (D-037).
- Languages and retention depend on results and leases already existing; translation is a result kind and retention is a deletion job under the same protocol (D-033).
- Desktop integration depends on capture and delivery only; each player adapter (D-025) is independent of everything else.

## Acceptance evidence by area

Each area is accepted on evidence approved by the owner named in D-035, against behavior tables written before the tests.

- Store and run machine: the recovery outcome for every non-terminal state, including diarizing and noting, asserted after a kill at that state boundary, matching the approved table.
- Capture: the F3 loss bound within its approved range, a decodable artifact whose packet count matches the durable prefix after every injected kill including kills during finalization and during recovery, and the measured sealer backlog under contention.
- Delivery: the dated F4 matrix, automated permission-matrix tests, the attempt-state and per-rung tables exercised including equal-length replacement, delayed-consumer paste and focus change between rungs, and a crash-during-delivery test showing needs_review with no re-post.
- Recognition: word error rate rows attached to machine, model revision, quantization and runtime revision, plus the memory slope at three durations measured inside the service.
- Vocabulary: table-driven determinism across match precedence, ordering, boundaries, case and scripts without spaces.
- Modes: human rubric scores on the fidelity corpus including adversarial cases, scored under the rule in verification, plus per-mode violation, checks_partial and prose-hold rates.
- Models: crash injection between blob rename and the activation transaction, activation while a run holds a lease, an import with no benchmark row that activates and is labeled unmeasured, an asset-level change that produces a different installation identity, archive and restore with History rows still resolving, and a complete session with the network denied.
- Mode rules and context: a dated browser URL matrix, rule-shadowing tests, tests that every source reaches the prompt as a term list unless the mode opts into prose, and retained-context lifecycle tests including deletion with the recording.
- Input sources: resident size at 10 minutes, 1 hour and 3 hours in both processes with the fitted slope reported, concurrent-session limits enforced, and a failed import leaving its source byte-identical.
- Meetings: two-stream alignment drift against its approved range, diarization error rate on a labeled internal set, the share of segments carrying unknown confidence, and provenance tests showing that renaming a speaker or re-running diarization leaves an existing note's text and pinned inputs unchanged while History flags the drift.
- History: deletion and retention race tests against live leases, and provenance tests over two recognition runs and two diarization runs of one recording.
- Desktop: a manual matrix over a music player, a browser tab and a video conferencing application, recording which had an adapter, what paused automatically, what resumed automatically, and what required the user action.

## Adding a new input source

A new source implements AudioSource, emitting timestamped native frames plus a SourceDescriptor giving live or seekable, clock domain, known duration, native rate and channel layout, and whether it honors credit. Arming branches on live against seekable, because a live source resolves a delivery target and is exempt from admission while a seekable source takes an ingest slot. The alternative considered was a pipeline per source, each owning its chunking, conversion and cancellation. That is shorter today and duplicates the parts most likely to be wrong: a memory bug on long input would exist only in the import path, and cancellation semantics would drift between paths. The cost of one port is that every source carries timing metadata even when it has one stream and no drift.

## Replacing a model runtime

Runtimes are separate adapter targets and separate service binaries, each publishing a capability descriptor with measured fields, a revision and a parameter schema. results.params_json stores parameters under a stable application-level schema with a runtime-specific extension blob, and results.params_rendered stores the human-readable form produced at insert time, so History rows from a removed runtime stay readable after its presentation hook is gone. The settings interface renders common parameters, meaning context length, temperature, beam size, thread count and quantization, generically from that schema, and a runtime may supply presentation hooks for parameters with conditional validity, model-specific ranges or memory effects. Replacing a runtime therefore adds a bounded amount of interface work; a claim that a schema removes bespoke interface work entirely would be too strong.

Storage effect of a swap is bounded by D-038 rather than by garbage collection alone. History results reference their installations permanently, so an installation row is never unreferenced and collection by reference count would retain every superseded model. Archiving separates the two: the row, hashes, capabilities and notices stay, the assets are released, and History states that reprocessing through that installation needs them restored. Removing an adapter does not delete anything by itself: its installations move to orphaned_runtime, stay installed, and appear in the model manager with their size and an archive action, plus a launch-time notice listing them. Deletion of weights is always a user action.

Calling a runtime API directly from feature code removes a layer. Under that arrangement, swapping runtimes touches every call site, the settings interface and the persisted parameters, and old History rows referencing removed parameter names become uninterpretable. RESEARCH flags long-recording behavior and integration cost as unexamined for both speech candidates, so designing as though the first choice is permanent would be the wrong bet.

## Maintenance costs accepted

- GRDB: a dependency with its own release cadence plus migration discipline, paid for by FTS5 and tested migrations.
- Vendored C and C++ runtimes: long builds, periodic vendoring and upstream API drift. Pinned to tagged revisions with an update checklist that reruns the evaluation harness, refreshes capability descriptors and bumps the recorded runtime revision.
- Accessibility insertion and delivery profiles: per-application behavior is undocumented and changes. The matrix is re-run per macOS minor release and per major update of the applications in it, and the result is a dated table in the repository. Because rung 3 is reachable only through a profile entry, an unmaintained profile degrades to unconfirmed outcomes rather than to duplicated text.
- Player adapters: one integration per supported player, each with its own automation permission and its own breakage risk on player updates. Players without an adapter get the explicit user action, so an unmaintained adapter degrades to a manual step.
- Validator language packs: each language needs segmentation, interrogative detection and a content-word list, plus rubric review in that language. Languages without a pack run the language-independent set and take the disposition in D-012.
- Chunk journal and finalization: extra file management, two fsyncs per chunk period per stream, and a recovery sequence that must stay idempotent. It buys a recovery story that does not depend on a container surviving a kill.
- XPC services: five bundles to sign, entitlement sets to keep correct, and interruption handling in the client. A missing entitlement fails closed.
- Container materialization, if F2 selects it for a runtime: a second copy of that runtime's weights per service, which the model manager reports as part of library size.

## What supporting other Macs would require

Intel support means the whisper.cpp adapter with its own model format, a smaller generation model, its own memory budget and its own evaluation run; RESEARCH notes that documented platform support does not establish comparable performance. Machines with 8 GB need a smaller pairing and a residency policy that unloads the speech model before loading the generation model, at the cost of latency between stages, with diarization sequential to both and the preview slot disabled. Both are adapter and policy changes and neither touches the store or the run machine.

## Who decides what correct means (D-035)

A passing test shows the implementation met its assertions under the tested conditions; the assertions can encode a wrong expectation. Expected behavior is therefore written and approved before tests are written. docs/behavior/ holds a table per subsystem giving, for each state and event pair, the expected next state, the persisted effect and the user-visible effect. Cancellation at every stage, permission loss per capability, focus change during a delivery sequence, crash at each boundary including finalization, lease conflict, service interruption, admission and shedding, and check disposition are events in those tables. Every row cites a SPEC.md clause; rows with no clause are marked derived and need explicit approval. The normative approver is the user as product owner, or a delegate named in docs/behavior/OWNERS; independent authorship is a hygiene rule and carries no authority. Tests reference row identifiers, and changing an approved row requires re-approval recorded in git history.

The same approver signs each measurement range below before its gate runs, and the rubric rule before the fidelity corpus is scored. Each range is recorded with its basis and its approval status, so a number derived from a design parameter is distinguishable from a product target with no measurement behind it. Every range listed here is currently proposed and unapproved.

## Automated checks

- Run state machine property tests over every state and event pair including generated random sequences, asserting invariants: no delivery without a previously committed delivery_attempts row; no results row for a run cancelled before sealing; an artifact exists on disk exactly when its row says so; results.text is never updated; every non-recognition result has a primary input belonging to the same recording; every notes result has result_dependencies rows naming a diarization result and an assignment revision; every notes run's manifest pins inputs that committed before the run started.
- Provenance tests: re-recognize a recording under a second speech model and re-diarize it, then generate notes from each combination, and assert that every artifact resolves to exactly one transcript, one diarization result, one assignment revision, one installation and one runtime revision per stage.
- Meeting provenance drift: generate notes, rename a speaker, re-run diarization, and assert the note text and its pinned inputs are unchanged while History reports the drift and offers regeneration as a new run.
- Crash injection: SIGKILL at each stage boundary, including diarizing and noting, relaunch, and assert the recovery outcome named in the approved table, including no automatic re-delivery after a kill during delivering, no automatic notes run after a kill following a meeting's diarization commit, and idempotent re-sealing after a kill during sealing.
- Capture finalization: kills at every finalization write boundary and during recovery itself, asserting that repeated recovery converges, that a partially written packet table or size patch is discarded, and that surviving journal chunks are incorporated before the final table is committed.
- Pre-commit disposition: cancel during arming, capturing and sealing, kill the process before the sweep, relaunch, and assert the manifest disposition determines the outcome with no orphaned session directory.
- Deletion and retention races: a deterministic scheduler test that deletes a recording, and separately runs an age policy and an audio-discard policy, while a worker and a player hold leases; asserts that commits abort, no rows appear, scratch is removed, retention defers, and playback is not interrupted. A suspended holder whose process is alive must not have its lease reclaimed.
- Delivery predicate and rung suite: for each attempt state, focus outcome and rung, assert the target resolved, the revalidation performed, the signal evaluated and the transition taken. Cases include replacing a selection with text of identical length; an unrelated edit changing the value; a target with no readable value; a paste consumed after the readback, which must remain unconfirmed and must not reach rung 3; an accessibility error before any effect, which must reach rung 2; focus changing between rungs and before Return, which must end unconfirmed with no submission; and submission firing only after a confirmed delivery to a revalidated target.
- Pasteboard suite: restore only after confirmed delivery with changeCount unchanged; no restore after unconfirmed; user-triggered restore; refusal to snapshot above the configured limit with the user told first.
- Service isolation (F2): from inside each running inference service, attempt an outbound connection to a remote host and to a listening local socket and assert both fail; attempt a write outside the job scratch directory and assert it fails; repeat from the external decoder the decode service spawns; and load each model kind by all three access mechanisms. Build checks that service targets and their dependency closure import no networking modules, a symbol scan of the linked binaries, and a static check that fails the build if a runtime is constructed through an initializer that can download are corroborating evidence only; RESEARCH states that a symbol scan cannot establish that a process lacks network access, so the denial assertion inside the sandboxed process is the evidence that carries the claim.
- Offline session: a dictation, an import, a meeting with diarization and notes, and a model load under a network-denied profile, asserting no failure and no attempted connection.
- Long-input memory and admission: imports at 10 minutes, 1 hour and 3 hours, sampling resident size of the app and of the speech service, asserting a per-duration ceiling and a fitted slope within measurement noise; plus tests that a second live capture trigger is refused, that ingest slots bound concurrent imports, and that non-model resident memory stays under its stated ceiling.
- Scheduler tests: an interactive run arming while a batch speech job holds the slot must preempt it and obtain a preview rung; a batch job without verified checkpoint equivalence must restart whole rather than resume; the sealer shed sequence must fire at its stated backlog thresholds.
- Prompt-injection corpus: clipboard, screen and focused-element context containing instruction-shaped text, asserting that distillation removes the instruction sentences on the default path, that the context overlap check holds on the prose path, that the transcript survives, and that a prose run without an available language-dependent set holds the generated text rather than delivering it.
- Check disposition: for each mode and language pair without a pack, assert the generated result is produced and retained with checks_partial and the check list, that the delivered text is the normalized transcript for a mode declaring answersQuestions false, that no setting changes that, and that a mode revision declaring answersQuestions true delivers generated text and is shown as such in the mode indicator.
- Vocabulary determinism: match precedence, longest match with list-order tie-break, ICU word boundaries, case handling, scripts without spaces and post-generation reapplication, table-driven.
- Model lifecycle: crash injection between blob rename and the activation transaction; activation while a run holds a lease on the previous installation; garbage collection with and without live leases; an import with no benchmark row asserting that activation succeeds and the interface labels quality unmeasured; a tokenizer or template change producing a different installation identity; archive an installation and assert History rows still render from params_rendered while reprocessing is refused with a restore offer; adapter removal moving installations to orphaned_runtime without deleting anything; notices surviving archiving.
- Retained context: opt-in retention writes an artifact and a row, both removed with the recording and by retention policies; opt-out leaves only a digest; reprocessing a recording with no retained context reports it.
- Schema migration from fixture databases at each prior version.
- Leading audio: synthesize a trigger followed immediately by speech and assert the pre-roll ring contributes the leading audio to the journal, with the measured device-start latency recorded as the residual loss.
- Panel placement restore across display reconfiguration, including a removed display and an off-screen frame.

## Human review where assertions are weak

Transformation fidelity is reviewed and not only asserted. A fixed corpus of 40 recordings per mode per shipped language has expected outputs, scored against five criteria: meaning preserved, no invented facts, questions still questions, vocabulary terms intact, formatting within the declared contract. Each criterion is scored 0, 1 or 2 against a written definition of each level. Two reviewers score independently, neither being the author of the mode under review; where they differ by more than one point on any criterion a third reviewer adjudicates and that score stands.

The ship rule for a built-in mode revision: no item may score 0 on meaning preserved, no invented facts, or questions still questions, and no more than 10 percent of items may score 1 on any criterion. The structure of that rule is derived from the specification, which forbids inventing content and forbids answering a dictated question outside a mode that declares it; the 10 percent figure and the corpus size are proposals with no empirical basis, and 40 items resolves a violation rate only to roughly plus or minus 9 points at 95 percent confidence, which detects gross failures rather than small differences. A revision that fails is revised and re-scored; a built-in that cannot meet the rule is not shipped as a built-in and the reason is recorded. The corpus includes adversarial cases built to pass lexical checks while changing meaning: removed or inserted negation, swapped quantities, modality changes such as must to may, swapped attribution between two named people, an answer appended after a retained question, a sentence copied from the context block, and an instruction in prose context obeyed in words absent from that context.

Meeting notes are scored on the same scale with citation validity checked automatically and the uncited-bullet drop rate tracked; a note whose bullets cite segments that do not support them scores 0 on no invented facts.

Practical behavior in other macOS applications is verified by running the delivery matrix by hand across TextEdit, Mail, Notes, Safari plain input and contenteditable, Chrome, Xcode, Terminal, VS Code, Slack, Messages and Figma. Each cell records whether rung 1 is supported and preserved existing field content; whether the confirmation predicate is evaluable; whether any rejection signal exists that would justify a rung 3 profile entry; insertion at a caret in the middle of existing text; replacement of an active selection with equal-length and different-length text; paste with a delayed consumer; pasteboard state after an unconfirmed outcome; non-Latin text covering Japanese, Arabic in a right-to-left field, combining marks and emoji; behavior with an input method active; secure fields; and focus changing while events are being posted. The table is dated and re-run on macOS updates.

## Measurement protocols, ranges, basis and actions

No benchmark here has been executed. Each protocol is defined so that results, when they exist, are attributable, and each carries a range, the basis of that range and the action if it is missed. These govern shipped defaults; they never gate a compatible model the user imports.

- F1 recognition. Word error rate by language on a public set and an internal 60-utterance set, recording machine, memory, macOS version, runtime revision, model revision and quantization. Range: the default installation is no more than 15 percent relative worse than the comparison harness running an equivalent model, defined as the same upstream Whisper checkpoint at the nearest available quantization in each format, with both recorded. Basis: a margin proposed to tolerate format and quantization differences; no empirical basis.
