The comparison is executable because F1 builds the measurement-only whisper.cpp harness in the same gate, so the criterion does not depend on first shipping the adapter it might select. Action on failure: promote the harness to a shipping adapter and re-select the default pairing.
- F1 latency. Stop to final transcript for a 30-second utterance, p50 at most 3.0 s and p95 at most 6.0 s on the evaluation target, over at least 20 runs. Basis: product targets chosen by the designer with no measurement; approval or revision by the owner is what makes them binding. Action on failure: change the default model size or quantization; if no default meets them, publish the measured figure and drop the target rather than concealing it.
- F1 memory. Fitted slope of peak service resident size against input duration not distinguishable from zero at 95 percent confidence, with an absolute ceiling of 500 MB growth from the 10-minute to the 3-hour peak. Basis: the slope criterion follows from the credit window, which bounds in-flight audio to roughly 8 MB per session regardless of duration, so a correct implementation should be flat; the 500 MB ceiling is slack for allocator behavior with no measurement behind it. Action on failure: reduce the credit window and re-measure; if the slope persists, imports move to the comparison adapter.
- F1 preview arm. For each rung of the D-011 ladder: first provisional text visible within 1.5 s of speech onset, updates at least every 2 s, zero dropped capture frames over a 10-minute capture, and no change in final word error rate beyond measurement noise. Basis: the latency figures are designer proposals; the dropped-frame and final-quality criteria are derived from the requirement that the preview must not damage the recording it previews. Action: use the highest rung that passes; if no rung passes, that is a release question for the owner, not removal of the preview.
- F1 descriptors. Cancellation latency at p50 and p95, transcript equivalence after preemption and resume, peak service resident size and Metal heap peak per installation. Absence of verified checkpoint equivalence keeps whole-job restart (D-004).
- F3 capture. Maximum lost interval at most 4 seconds across at least 200 randomized kills, every recovery decoding end to end, and repeated recovery converging. Basis: derived, as two chunk periods at the default 2-second period. Action on failure: shorten the chunk period to 1 second and re-measure; if reconstruction is ever invalid, adopt the retain-until-verified fallback in D-030.
- F3 sealer. Unsealed backlog stays under 30 seconds of audio per live stream with one concurrent import and a loaded CPU, and the shed sequence fires at its thresholds. Basis: derived from the journal storage bound the capture design assumes. Action on failure: reduce ingest slots to zero during live capture, and if the backlog persists, raise the encode priority or lower the encode cost by reducing the sealed sample rate for meetings.
- F5 diarization inventory. Field list, centroid availability per fixture, segmenter and embedder resident size and wall time. No pass or fail; the result sets the meeting schema and the residency numbers.
- Diarization quality. Diarization error rate on a labeled internal meeting set, the share of segments carrying unknown confidence, whether centroid distance is monotone with correctness on cross-recording pairs, and behavior under speaker echo without headphones. Range: if DER exceeds 30 percent, the shipped default for meetings is diarization off with channel labels only, with the feature still present and user-enablable. Basis: above roughly one segment in three mislabeled, correcting by hand costs more than assigning from scratch; the figure is a proposal. This decides a default, not availability, and no imported model is gated by it.
- Two-stream alignment. Drift between microphone and system streams over a 60-minute meeting measured against injected reference tones. Range: at most 50 ms residual after host-time alignment. Basis: derived, since the smallest unit the product exposes is a segment boundary and a citation timestamp at second granularity, so 50 ms is well inside what any displayed artifact resolves. Action on failure: apply tone-derived linear drift correction at seal time; if residual drift still exceeds the range, reconsider the macOS 15 unified capture stream under D-001.

Until a measurement exists, the interface reports language support as declared by the model publisher and marked unmeasured, and no latency claim appears in the product.
assumptions: Deployment baseline is macOS 14.0. Basis: RESEARCH records macOS 14 and Xcode 16 among the prerequisites of the Argmax Swift package selected in D-020 and D-023, and ScreenCaptureKit system-audio capture predates 14, so nothing in the capture path needs a higher floor. Reconsider if the Argmax dependency is dropped, which lets the floor fall to whatever the remaining APIs need, or if measured two-stream drift exceeds its range and forces the WWDC24 unified microphone and system stream, which raises the floor to macOS 15.

Apple Silicon with 16 GB is the evaluation target and Intel is unsupported in the first release. Basis: the specification names the evaluation target; the first-release limit is an engineering decision recorded in D-001, taken because a second architecture doubles the evaluation burden before the primary target has any measurement, and RESEARCH notes that documented platform support does not establish comparable performance. Reconsider when an Intel requirement is confirmed; the work is a second adapter, a model pairing, a memory budget and a separate evaluation run.

A sandboxed XPC service with the network client entitlement withheld can load model weights and run Core ML and Metal inference through at least one of three access mechanisms: opened file descriptors, a read-only path exception scoped to Models/blobs, or materialization by the service inside its own container. Basis: Apple's XPC guide describes per-service sandboxes, Core ML and Metal execution needs no exception, and a service may always write and read inside its own container, so the third mechanism depends on no entitlement the design cannot grant; none of the three has been verified for these runtimes here. Reconsider at gate F2. There is no fallback outside the boundary: a runtime that cannot load under any mechanism is replaced by the alternative adapter behind the same port, and a model kind with no adapter that fits is escalated to the product owner as a specification question.

Model residency fits an 8 GB application budget on the 16 GB target: a turbo-class speech model at roughly 0.8 to 1.6 GB of weights, an optional preview-class speech model under 400 MB, an 8B-class generation model at 4-bit quantization at roughly 4.5 to 5 GB, a few hundred MB of key-value cache at 8k context, and under 200 MB of non-model ingest memory across the bounded session count. Basis: published quantized file sizes, credit-window arithmetic, and standard cache arithmetic, with no measured resident size and no accounting for runtime workspaces or Metal heaps. Reconsider at the first F1 descriptor, which reports process resident size and Metal peak; refusals state whether their numbers are measured or declared.

The diarization model set is small relative to the speech and generation models, in the tens to low hundreds of megabytes of weights for a pyannote-class segmenter, embedder and clusterer. Basis: published file sizes for models of that family; the resident cost of the specific Core ML conversions at the configured concurrency is unmeasured. Reconsider at F5, which records resident size and wall time; until then admission uses declared sizes plus a 100 percent margin and says so, and diarization is refused concurrency with generation.

The maximum audio loss after an abrupt termination is one chunk period plus unflushed data within it. Basis: chunks are written, fsynced and renamed individually, encoded bytes are fsynced before the index record that names them, the index record carries a CRC and per-packet sizes, and finalization commits through a seal record, so recovery depends on records the application wrote itself instead of on a container surviving truncation. The exact bound has not been measured. Reconsider after F3; a worse bound is answered by shortening the chunk period, and an invalid reconstruction by retaining chunks until the artifact is verified.

ALAC encoding of a live capture runs far below realtime on the evaluation target, so the sealer keeps the unsealed backlog under 30 seconds without competing for admission. Basis: lossless encoding of 16 kHz mono, or of two native-rate meeting streams, is a small fraction of one core on Apple Silicon by the arithmetic of sample rate and packet size; unmeasured under contention. Reconsider at F3's contention measurement; the shed sequence in D-004 is what bounds the failure if the assumption is wrong.

Prompt-based vocabulary biasing in the whisper family raises the chance a term is recognized and guarantees nothing. Basis: the mechanism is a decoder prompt instead of a decoding constraint, and the prompt slot is bounded at roughly 224 tokens. The product text says exactly that. Reconsider if a runtime exposes real biasing or constrained decoding, which moves exact-name handling into recognition.

Lexical and structural checks on generated text are necessary conditions on transformation fidelity and not a proof that a mode obeyed its contract, and on a prose context path an instruction obeyed in new words is undetectable by every check listed. Basis: content-word recall, interrogative survival, expansion ratio and context n-gram overlap can all pass on text whose meaning changed. Reconsider if the adversarial fidelity corpus finds a class of violations that survives every check, which would argue for a sampled semantic check by a second model despite its cost and its shared failure mode.

Leaving the dictated transcript on the pasteboard after an unconfirmed delivery is preferable to restoring the previous contents on a timer. Basis: the prior review established that any fixed delay races a delayed consumer, and losing the user's text is worse than leaving the pasteboard changed; the panel states the pasteboard holds the transcript and offers Restore clipboard. Reconsider if F4 finds a target class where consumption can be acknowledged, which lets restore run automatically for those targets.

A CoreAudio device-is-running flag on the default output device is evidence that something is playing and is not evidence of ownership, of the recipient of a media key, or of any pause. Basis: it is a public property needing no private framework, and it identifies neither the playing application nor the effect of a posted key. It is therefore used only to decide whether to offer the user the manual Pause media action, and never to post a key automatically. Reconsider if a supported system API supplies playing-application identity and pause confirmation without a per-player integration.

AVFoundation covers the initial import format matrix: wav, aiff, caf, mp3, m4a in AAC and ALAC, mp4, m4v and mov. Basis: system decoder coverage. Reconsider at the first refusal, with opus in webm or matroska the likely ones, at which point the user-selected external decoder running inside the sandboxed decode service is the documented path.

FTS5 is compiled into the system SQLite on the deployment baseline. Basis: it has shipped enabled for several macOS releases, though this is a build-setup check and not a verified fact here. Reconsider immediately if the check fails; the fallback is GRDB against a bundled SQLite, which increases binary size and adds an update obligation.

Separate microphone and system-audio streams give better attribution than diarizing a mixed stream, and channel origin is a fact about capture instead of a claim about who spoke. Basis: structural, since the two capture paths exist and channel origin is certain, while echo from speakers into the microphone is not accounted for by structure alone. Reconsider after diarization and echo evaluation; if a mixed-stream diarizer performs comparably, the second stream becomes an optimization.

The diarizer supplies cluster boundaries and centroid embeddings with cosine-distance helpers, supplies no per-segment confidence or margin, and may supply no centroid for a given speaker. Basis: stated in RESEARCH for SpeakerKit v1.1.0's DiarizationResult declaration, from source inspection with no inference experiment run. The schema therefore stores per-segment calibrated confidence as unknown, stores no per-segment margin, and uses centroid distance only for cross-recording identity proposals the user confirms. Reconsider at F5, which inventories the fields actually exposed at the pinned version.

Lossless 16 kHz mono audio at roughly 50 to 60 MB per hour makes indefinite dictation retention acceptable by default, while native-rate meeting streams are large enough to surface in the library size view. Basis: arithmetic from 16-bit PCM at 115 MB per hour and typical lossless ratios. Reconsider when a library crosses a user-visible size threshold, at which point the retention interface is surfaced instead of a default quietly applied.

A 200 ms arming budget is tolerable for mode resolution, target resolution and context sampling, and context sources missing it are skipped for that run. Basis: a design choice about perceived responsiveness with no user study; audio capture does not wait on it because the pre-roll ring starts at the trigger, so the budget affects context completeness rather than lost speech. Reconsider if screen-context sampling routinely misses the deadline and users want it, which moves sampling off the arming path and makes the rewrite stage wait for it.

The pasteboard snapshot limit of 10 MB is a starting value, not a measured threshold. Basis: chosen to avoid duplicating large images and file promises in memory during a latency-sensitive operation, with no measurement of snapshot cost. It is a configurable setting, and F4 records snapshot time by content type so the default can be set from data. Reconsider once that measurement exists.

Retained context text, captured audio and transcripts are protected by file-system permissions and whatever full-disk encryption the user has enabled, not by application-level encryption. Basis: consistency with the rest of the library, which has the same exposure, and the absence of a stated threat model that separates context from audio. Reconsider if a threat model asks for at-rest encryption, which would apply to the library as a whole rather than to context alone.

Weights the application offers for download are limited to assets whose notices permit redistribution, and everything else is user-imported. Basis: RESEARCH records the WhisperKit model card as MIT and records component-specific notices for the diarization collection referring to WeSpeaker and VBx. Reconsider per asset as the notice inventory is compiled; an asset that cannot be offered stays importable, so no feature depends on the outcome.

decisions.title: macOS baseline and hardware target
decisions.choice: Deployment target macOS 14.0 and Apple Silicon for the first release, with later-OS APIs gated at runtime and never required.
decisions.rationale: The speech runtime selected in D-020 and the diarizer in D-023 ship in one Swift package whose prerequisites RESEARCH records as macOS 14 and Xcode 16, so the floor follows a dependency the design has committed to. ScreenCaptureKit system-audio capture is available at 14; the WWDC24 microphone stream output arrived later, and microphone capture uses AVAudioEngine on every supported version, so the newer output is off the critical path. Apple Silicon only in the first release is an engineering decision, not a reading of the specification: a second architecture requires its own model format, its own memory budget and its own evaluation run, and doing that before the primary target has any measurement spends effort on a comparison neither side of which is known.

alternatives.option: Baseline macOS 15 for the unified ScreenCaptureKit microphone and system-audio stream
alternatives.tradeoff: One capture path and a shared clock for meetings, at the cost of excluding Sonoma users for a convenience the two-stream design handles with host-time alignment and tone-derived drift correction.

alternatives.option: Baseline macOS 13
alternatives.tradeoff: Wider reach; falls below the selected package's stated prerequisite and adds an operating system to the support matrix that nothing is evaluated on.

alternatives.option: Ship Intel and Apple Silicon together
alternatives.tradeoff: Broader hardware coverage; doubles the evaluation burden that RESEARCH warns documentation cannot substitute for, and forces a second model tier before the primary target is measured.

decisions.consequences: Meetings align two streams by host time instead of receiving them from one, and the alignment range in verification is what decides whether that holds. Intel users wait for the second speech adapter and its own evaluation, and the reason is recorded here rather than attributed to the specification. Any API newer than 14 sits behind an availability check with a defined fallback.
decisions.reconsider_when: The Argmax dependency is dropped, measured two-stream drift exceeds its range after correction, or an Intel requirement is confirmed.

decisions.title: Package layout and dependency direction
decisions.choice: One SPM package with a pure core, a ports target of protocols and value types, a validation target holding transformation contracts and language packs, adapter targets per external concern, service targets for inference, and a thin Xcode app shell as the composition root. Core depends only on ports; nothing depends on an adapter except the shell.
decisions.rationale: The scope includes a speech runtime that may be replaced, four input sources, a diarizer, and an insertion mechanism whose behavior varies per target application. Each is an adapter. Keeping the run state machine, mode resolution, the vocabulary pipeline, delivery policy and contract checking free of system frameworks is what lets the earliest work exercise cancel, crash, delete-during-processing, delivery ladders and retention races before any runtime or window server is involved. Service logic living in library targets keeps it inside swift test even though the bundles are produced by Xcode.

alternatives.option: Single application target with feature folders
alternatives.tradeoff: Faster early progress; every behavioral test then needs permissions and real models, and swapping a runtime touches feature code throughout.

alternatives.option: Separate SPM packages per subsystem in a workspace
alternatives.tradeoff: Stronger boundaries and independent versioning, at the cost of cross-package version churn for a single application with one consumer.

decisions.consequences: Adapters need explicit wiring in the shell and value types at the boundary in place of framework types passed around. The application bundle cannot come from swift build alone, so there are two entry points: swift test for logic and the Xcode scheme for the shipping application and its signed services.
decisions.reconsider_when: The port boundary starts needing per-adapter escape hatches that leak framework types into core, which would mean the abstraction is fighting the domain.

decisions.title: Inference runs in bundled sandboxed XPC services, one per model kind, with three model-access mechanisms
decisions.choice: Speech recognition, generation, diarization and optional external decoding each run in a bundled XPC service, sandboxed on its own with com.apple.security.network.client withheld. Model assets reach a service by opened file descriptors, by a read-only path exception scoped to Models/blobs, or by materialization inside the service's own container, whichever F2 shows the runtime needs. No inference runs in the app process and nothing listens on a port. There is no unsandboxed inference service.
decisions.rationale: RESEARCH's follow-up records that bundled services have separate sandboxes, that a service can fail or be terminated independently of its client, and that signed services with network entitlements withheld are the thing to evaluate for inference; it also states that a scan for socket symbols cannot establish that a process lacks network access. A withheld entitlement is a property of the process, so it covers linked frameworks and dynamically loaded code that a scan cannot reach. Three access mechanisms are named because the previous revision made a failed access method a reason to leave the boundary, which put the offline contract at the mercy of a loader detail; the third mechanism needs no exception at all, so loading failure is a runtime-selection problem rather than a boundary problem. Diarization gets its own service because RESEARCH records that its runtime's default initialization may download models, and because it loads a different model set whose residency is counted separately (D-027).

alternatives.option: Fall back to an unsandboxed service when sandboxed loading fails
alternatives.tradeoff: Guarantees some runtime can always be used; replaces system-enforced egress denial with a symbol scan that RESEARCH rejects as evidence, so the local-only requirement would rest on weaker evidence during routine operation.

alternatives.option: Child helper processes over an inherited socket pair
alternatives.tradeoff: Full control of launch and lifecycle with no launchd involvement; provides no system-level egress denial.

alternatives.option: Link the runtimes into the application process
alternatives.tradeoff: Lowest latency and no serialization boundary; a native crash kills the app mid-run and address-space growth from model loading persists for the process lifetime.

alternatives.option: Run diarization inside SpeechService
alternatives.tradeoff: One fewer bundle to sign; couples two model sets in one residency slot and gives the runtime with documented implicit-download behavior the same process as the one without it.

alternatives.option: Run the upstream HTTP server on localhost
alternatives.tradeoff: Reuses upstream tooling; opens a port every local process can reach and turns the offline property into a claim about configuration the app does not own.

decisions.consequences: Connection interruption is a normal event: the run fails at its stage, committed results stand, and the next admission rebuilds the service. Audio windows cross the connection under credit, so the memory ceiling is measured in each service as well as the app. If F2 selects container materialization for a runtime, that runtime's weights exist twice on disk and the model manager reports it. Five bundles are signed with their own entitlement sets, and a missing entitlement fails closed.
decisions.reconsider_when: F2 shows a runtime cannot load under any of the three mechanisms, which selects the alternative adapter behind the same port rather than relaxing the boundary.

decisions.title: Concurrency, lanes, admission of non-model work, and interactive slot reservation
decisions.choice: One actor per processing run owning its state and rows; a real-time audio callback writing into lock-free rings; a single ResourceScheduler actor with a capture lane, an interactive lane and a batch lane. Live capture writing and incremental sealing are exempt from admission and run above batch quality of service, bounded instead by one concurrent live capture session. Seekable ingest is admitted: an import's decoding, conversion, journaling and sealing occupy one of a bounded number of ingest slots, one by default. Model slots are speech-primary, speech-preview, generation and diarization, at most one occupant each, with admission also checking summed footprint against D-027. An interactive dictation run reserves the speech-primary slot from arming until its recognition result commits, preempting batch speech work. Preemption resumes from a checkpoint only where the runtime descriptor records verified equivalence; otherwise the batch job restarts whole. The sealer has a backlog bound of 30 seconds of audio per live stream with a shedding sequence: pause batch admission, then stop ingest, then stop capture and seal as interrupted.
decisions.rationale: The scope puts a latency-sensitive dictation path beside long batch work on a machine that cannot hold several models resident, so admission belongs in one testable place. The previous revision exempted capture from admission without saying which capture, which left an import's ingest path unaccounted while it entered the same capturing stage; the live and seekable distinction is the line that matters, because only a live source loses data when deferred. Reserving the speech-primary slot for interactive runs removes the contradiction where the preview ladder promised a fallback rung that could not run while batch work held the only speech slot. A quality-of-service level is not a guarantee, so the sealer gets a numeric backlog bound and a shedding sequence, which is also what makes cancellation during sealing bounded.

alternatives.option: Exempt all capture-stage work from admission
alternatives.tradeoff: One rule for a stage; unbounded concurrent imports each hold windows, journals and buffers outside any budget.

alternatives.option: Admit live capture like any other work
alternatives.tradeoff: Uniform accounting; a queued live capture loses audio that cannot be recovered.

alternatives.option: Serial queue, first come first served
alternatives.tradeoff: Predictable; the user waits behind a batch job, which is the failure the requirements care about most.

alternatives.option: Leave batch speech work running and let the preview wait
alternatives.tradeoff: Imports finish sooner; the recording display has no provisional text during exactly the runs that need it.

alternatives.option: Concurrent residency of every model kind with no admission control
alternatives.tradeoff: Better pipelining on a large machine; on the 16 GB target it invites swap.

decisions.consequences: A long import is interrupted whenever the user dictates, and restarts whole unless its descriptor allows resume; a setting lets the user prefer the import, at the cost of delaying the dictation. Batch workers need restart points either way. A second recording trigger during a live session is refused rather than queued. The audio callback thread has hard constraints that need review discipline.
decisions.reconsider_when: Descriptors show a runtime whose resume reproduces the unpreempted transcript, allowing cheaper preemption, or measurements show a machine class where concurrent residency fits and the single-slot rule costs latency for nothing.

decisions.title: Persistence: SQLite with FTS5 for metadata and text, files for audio and retained context
decisions.choice: SQLite through GRDB in WAL mode for metadata, runs, results, leases and result text, with FTS5 over result text; audio and retained context text in per-recording directories. Numbered migrations with fixture-based migration tests.
decisions.rationale: History requires search across transcripts and results, and FTS5 with bm25 ranking and snippets is the reason to prefer SQLite. Deletion during active work, lease acquisition and model activation all need a transaction that combines a check with a write. Keeping large text and audio out of the database keeps backup, integrity check and migration times short, and keeps retained context out of the search index so results are about the user's own speech.

alternatives.option: SwiftData
alternatives.tradeoff: Least code for models and views with native observation; no full-text index, and migration behavior is harder to test against fixtures for a schema that must survive many capability additions.

alternatives.option: Core Data with an external search index
alternatives.tradeoff: Mature and Apple-supported; adds a second index to keep consistent with deletions, which is the consistency problem the tombstone and lease rules exist to contain.

alternatives.option: Raw libsqlite3 with a hand-written wrapper
alternatives.tradeoff: No third-party dependency; reimplements migrations, statement caching and observation.

alternatives.option: JSON files per recording with an in-memory index
alternatives.tradeoff: Inspectable and easy to back up; search, leases and transactional deletion become bespoke, and the index is rebuilt every launch.

decisions.consequences: A dependency with its own release cadence and migration discipline. FTS triggers must stay in sync with result inserts and deletes, covered by tests. Database and files can disagree after a crash, which the recovery contract resolves.
decisions.reconsider_when: The system SQLite lacks FTS5 on the baseline, in which case GRDB is built against a bundled SQLite, or library sizes make a per-recording file layout with an external index preferable.

decisions.title: Processing runs as explicit state machines with a per-run settings snapshot
decisions.choice: A state machine per processing run over the stages idle, arming, capturing, sealing, recognizing, diarizing, refining, rewriting, noting, delivering and terminal, in the pure core, with a RunManifest written and fsynced at run start pinning mode revision, model installation ids, runtime and adapter revisions, vocabulary revision, language setting, translation flag, validator pack set and, for reprocessing and notes, the parent inputs. A run visits only the stages its kind declares. Run kinds are dictation, import, meeting, notes, reprocess_recognition, reprocess_diarization and reprocess_text. Microphone capture starts at the trigger into a pre-roll ring, so arming work runs concurrently with capture.
decisions.rationale: The manifest is what makes settings snapshots real: a run reads its manifest and never live settings, so editing a mode or switching models mid-run cannot change what a result means. Notes are a separate run kind rather than a tail stage of the meeting run because a manifest is fsynced at run start and the diarization result and assignment revision do not exist then; a run cannot pin inputs that will exist later, and recovery from noting reads that manifest to know what stood. Attaching the machine to a run instead of to a recording is what lets one recording carry several recognitions and several diarizations without ambiguity. Starting capture at the trigger removes the case where a push-to-talk user speaks during arming and loses the first word.

alternatives.option: Read live settings at each stage
alternatives.tradeoff: No snapshot machinery; a mode edit during a long recognition silently changes the result's meaning.

alternatives.option: One meeting run through noting with a manifest extension committed before noting
alternatives.tradeoff: One run per meeting and a simpler list; the manifest stops being a single fsynced snapshot and recovery has to reason about which extension was durable.

alternatives.option: Implicit state through nullable columns
alternatives.tradeoff: Fewer types; illegal states become representable and per-stage cancellation loses its single definition point.

alternatives.option: One state machine per recording
alternatives.tradeoff: Simpler list view; a second recognition has nowhere to live and reprocessing has to mutate the recording's state.

decisions.consequences: A meeting produces at least two runs, which the detail view groups. If the app crashes between a meeting's diarization commit and the creation of its notes run, recovery does not start generation; History shows notes not generated with a Generate action. Settings changes take effect on the next run, which the interface shows. The pre-roll ring holds audio before any mode decision, so cancellation during arming discards it explicitly.
decisions.reconsider_when: A requirement needs mid-run settings changes, such as switching language during a long meeting, which would need a segmented manifest in place of one per run.

decisions.title: Cancellation contract defined for every stage a run can occupy
decisions.choice: A stage-indexed table of cancellation effects enforced in core and shown in the panel, covering arming, capturing, sealing, recognizing, diarizing, refining, rewriting, noting and delivering, as listed under failure behavior. Cancelling a reprocess or notes run leaves every earlier run's results intact.
decisions.rationale: The specification requires defined effects at every processing stage. Four judgment calls carry the table: sealing runs to completion because it is bounded by the backlog rule in D-004, idempotent, and needed for any disposition to be coherent; recognizing saves no partial transcript because a truncated transcript that looks complete is more damaging than an absent one; diarizing saves nothing partial for the same reason applied to segment coverage; rewriting keeps the normalized result because the expensive work is done and the user usually still wants their words.

alternatives.option: Cancel always discards everything
alternatives.tradeoff: One rule; throws away a completed recognition because the user did not want the rewrite.

alternatives.option: Cancel always keeps everything
alternatives.tradeoff: Nothing is lost; a sentence spoken into the wrong window persists to History.

alternatives.option: Abort sealing immediately on cancel
alternatives.tradeoff: Stops sooner; leaves a partially finalized artifact whose disposition and recovery both need special cases that idempotent completion avoids.

alternatives.option: Prompt at cancel time
alternatives.tradeoff: No wrong default; a modal on the escape path is when a user least wants a dialog.

decisions.consequences: Workers need checkpoints so cancel is prompt without being abrupt. Cancelling during sealing has a short wait bounded by the backlog rule, which the panel names with the current figure. The panel needs a per-stage message so the effect is visible when it happens.
decisions.reconsider_when: Usage shows repeated re-recording after cancels during recognition, which would argue for keeping partial transcripts clearly marked as partial.

decisions.title: Delivery target resolved once per focus outcome and revalidated before every posted event
decisions.choice: At arming, latch the frontmost process id, bundle identifier, window number, focused accessibility element and that element's readback capability. At delivery the target is resolved once: the latched element when it is still focused; the currently focused element when the latched application is frontmost with a different element focused and the per-mode follow-focus setting is on, which is the default; no target, meaning hold, when follow-focus is off, when another application is frontmost, or when the latched application quit. Immediately before each event-based rung and before the submit Return, the coordinator revalidates that the frontmost process, window number and focused element still equal the resolved target; a mismatch ends the attempt as unconfirmed with no retry and no submission. Re-focusing the latched target is opt-in. Only dictation runs deliver.
decisions.rationale: The intended target is the one the user was looking at when they started speaking, and the panel is non-activating (D-011) so showing it does not disturb the latch. Resolving one target per outcome removes the earlier contradiction between policy and mechanism. Resolution alone is not enough, because Command-V, synthesized typing and Return reach whatever is focused when each event is posted, and processing can take seconds; revalidation immediately before each event is what ties the resolved target to the event that acts on it. Holding instead of inserting into an unexpected application is conservative because text placed in the wrong window can be unrecoverable and can be sensitive, while a hold costs one click.

alternatives.option: Resolve once and post without revalidation
alternatives.tradeoff: Fewer accessibility round trips; a focus change between rungs sends text or a Return into an unrelated window.

alternatives.option: Always deliver into whatever is frontmost at delivery time
alternatives.tradeoff: No held results; text lands in the wrong application whenever focus changes during processing.

alternatives.option: Always act on the latched element regardless of focus
alternatives.tradeoff: One target for every case; writes into a field the user has left.

alternatives.option: Always hold and require confirmation
alternatives.tradeoff: Never wrong; adds a click to every dictation, which defeats the tool.

decisions.consequences: The panel needs a held state with actions and History must show undelivered results. Revalidation adds an accessibility query before each posted event, which is cheap compared with the insertion itself. The same-application default will occasionally insert into a different field in the same window, which matches clicking into the target field while speaking and is a per-mode setting for users who disagree.
decisions.reconsider_when: Holds fire often enough to annoy, which would argue for making opt-in re-focus the default for users who enable it.

decisions.title: Insertion ladder with rung-specific fallthrough and a content-based confirmation predicate
decisions.choice: Rung 1 sets AXSelectedText on the delivery target; AXValue is never set. A non-success AXError from that call is an explicit negative and is the only condition that permits rung 2, because that result is returned before any effect on the target. Rung 2 writes the pasteboard and posts Command-V; an unchanged readback is not an explicit negative, and rung 2 falls through to rung 3 only when the target's delivery profile records a target-specific rejection signal and that signal fires. Rung 3 synthesizes Unicode typing capped at 400 characters. Every rung is confirmed by one predicate: the expected text at the expected insertion location with the caret or selection immediately after it. Any outcome that is neither a confirmation nor that rung's own explicit negative is unconfirmed, which stops the ladder. The pasteboard is restored only after a confirmed delivery while the change count is ours, or on the user's explicit action.
decisions.rationale: RESEARCH distinguishes an accessibility object's value from its selected text and notes that setting an editable field's value can replace its contents, so insertion is a selection-aware operation. It also states that posting a paste event supplies no acknowledgment that the target consumed the clipboard, and REVIEW_NOTES records the delayed-consumer case directly: a target can apply the paste after any readback the app performs. Treating an unchanged readable value as rejection therefore reintroduces duplication, which is why fallthrough is now tied to what each mechanism can prove rather than to one shared signal. An accessibility error precedes any effect, so it is safe to fall through; a posted event has no such result, so only a signal specific to that target can license another attempt.

alternatives.option: Unchanged readable value counts as rejection
alternatives.tradeoff: Reaches more targets automatically; duplicates text whenever a consumer applies the paste after the readback, which is the recorded failure.

alternatives.option: Length or range comparison as the signal
alternatives.tradeoff: Works on targets exposing only a length; produces a false negative on equal-length replacement.

alternatives.option: Stop after rung 2 in all cases
alternatives.tradeoff: Never types; loses the one path that works in targets with no accessibility insertion and a rejecting paste handler.

alternatives.option: A dedicated input method
alternatives.tradeoff: The system-supported route for inserting text; requires the user to install and select an input method, changing their typing setup for a dictation feature.

decisions.consequences: Rung 3 is unreachable for any target without a profile entry, so synthesized typing becomes rare and the common uncertain outcome is unconfirmed with the transcript on the pasteboard. Delivery profiles become shipped data with a dated matrix and a maintenance obligation. Reading a value back costs an accessibility round trip, which a profile can cap by reading a window around the insertion point.
decisions.reconsider_when: F4 finds targets that expose a genuine rejection signal, which adds profile entries, or a supported API for inserting text into another application appears.

decisions.title: Delivery idempotency, a complete attempt-state table with per-rung records, and no automatic retry
decisions.choice: Commit a delivery_attempts row naming recording, result, run, target and state before any event is posted or any accessibility write is issued, and a delivery_attempt_rungs row per rung recording whether its external effect began, the signal observed and the outcome. States are pending, in_progress, delivered, rejected, unconfirmed, held, failed and needs_review. Terminal states are delivered, unconfirmed, held, failed and needs_review. On launch, pending, in_progress and unconfirmed become needs_review; delivered, held and failed are untouched. The app never re-posts automatically.
decisions.rationale: A paste into a target that cannot be read back gives no confirmation, so after a crash the app cannot distinguish delivered from about to deliver, and any automatic retry risks inserting the same paragraph twice. Committing before acting means recovery always sees an attempt was in flight. Per-rung records exist because the ladder can begin an external effect on one rung and stop on another; without them, recovery and the interface cannot say what the user should check.

alternatives.option: Retry pending deliveries on launch
alternatives.tradeoff: Recovers a crash before posting; duplicates text after posting, with no way to tell the cases apart.

alternatives.option: No attempt record, recover from run state
alternatives.tradeoff: One fewer table; the window between deciding to deliver and acting is exactly where a crash is unrecoverable without a durable record.

alternatives.option: One attempt row with no rung detail
alternatives.tradeoff: Simpler schema; a needs_review item cannot say which mechanism touched the target.

decisions.consequences: After a crash mid-delivery the user gets a needs_review item naming the last rung whose effect began, and decides. Re-delivery is always explicit. The state and rung tables are part of the approved behavior tables and are asserted transition by transition.
decisions.reconsider_when: A target class emerges whose consumption can be acknowledged, which would make a bounded automatic retry safe for those targets specifically.

decisions.title: Recording display as a non-activating panel, with a preview ladder that always produces text
decisions.choice: An NSPanel with nonactivating and borderless style, status-bar level, joining all spaces, movable by background, ordered front without becoming key. Provisional text renders in a secondary style with a live label; the final transcript replaces it in the primary style with a brief change highlight. The waveform is drawn from a 10 ms RMS and peak envelope computed allocation-free on the capture thread. Failures appear as a row with a short reason and one action. Placement is stored as a fraction of the display's visible frame plus the display identifier, clamped to the primary display when either is gone. Interactive runs reserve the speech-primary slot (D-004), and the preview ladder is: the primary model's streaming pass; a preview-class model under 400 MB in the speech-preview slot; batched updates at voice-activity pauses. Each rung must show first text within 1.5 s of speech onset, update at least every 2 s, drop no capture frames and leave final word error rate unchanged within noise. Waveform-only is not an accepted end state.
decisions.rationale: The panel must never become key, since activating it would break the delivery target that D-008 depends on. Provisional and final text are different artifacts, so they are shown differently and the provisional stream is never persisted. Fractional placement survives resolution and display changes. A provisional live transcript is a named requirement, so the earlier ladder was incomplete in a specific way: both of its rungs needed speech inference while the only speech slot could be held by batch work. Reserving the slot for interactive runs and giving the preview model its own capped slot is what makes the ladder executable. If no rung meets its criteria on the evaluation target, that is a release question for the product owner rather than a silent scope reduction.

alternatives.option: A normal SwiftUI window
alternatives.tradeoff: Standard behavior and less AppKit; it activates the application and changes the frontmost application, breaking delivery targeting.

alternatives.option: Menu bar popover only
alternatives.tradeoff: No extra window; anchored to the menu bar so it cannot sit near where the user is typing.

alternatives.option: Degrade to waveform and a voice-activity indicator
alternatives.tradeoff: Guarantees capture is never disturbed; drops a named requirement.

alternatives.option: Promote the provisional transcript as the final result
alternatives.tradeoff: Feels faster; delivers text produced from partial context as final.

decisions.consequences: A preview-class model is a second small installation to manage and to count in the budget, and the panel labels which rung is active. Panel focus and level behavior is AppKit-managed with SwiftUI content and needs its own tests. Users see text change when the final transcript arrives, which is highlighted rather than silent.
decisions.reconsider_when: Measurement shows the primary pass costs dropped buffers or final quality, which selects a lower rung rather than removing the preview.

decisions.title: Modes as versioned revisions with structured contracts, split check sets, and a stated disposition for every unchecked path
decisions.choice: Every mode carries a structured TransformationContract (allowed operations, an answersQuestions flag, a content bound expressed as a recall threshold or a citation requirement, the languages its validator supports, and per-source context representation) alongside its free-form prompt. Revisions are content-addressed and runs pin a revision id. The language-independent set always runs: expansion ratio, context overlap rejecting spans of eight or more tokens present in context and absent from the transcript, vocabulary survival, script sanity, and orthographic interrogative-marker detection reported as a signal. The language-dependent set needs a pack: interrogative survival in order, content-word recall, unsupported-sentence detection. An observed violation retries once with a stricter instruction and then delivers the normalized transcript, retaining the generated text marked contract_violation. Without a pack, the generated text is still produced, retained and one click from delivery, but for a mode declaring answersQuestions false the delivered text is the normalized transcript, with no override. Context is distilled to a capped term list per source by default, including focused-element text; prose is per-mode opt-in per source, and when any prose context is present automatic delivery additionally requires the language-dependent set to be available and to pass.
decisions.rationale: Prompt wording cannot enforce that a dictated question stays a question, so permitted transformations are a machine-checkable property with a defined failure path. The previous revision made the no-pack disposition turn on an interrogative marker while classifying interrogative detection as language-dependent, which left the protection resting on a check the run did not have; the marker check now exists in the independent set as a reported signal, and the disposition no longer depends on it, because a marker can show that a question exists and cannot show that none was asked. The override is removed because it let a mode declaring that it does not answer questions deliver unchecked rewrites, and the specification requires answering to be explicitly part of the selected mode. Context distillation moved to every source because the earlier asymmetry, distilling screen and clipboard while always passing focused-element text as prose, had no stated reason: a focused field can hold text written by someone else. Where prose is genuinely needed, the disposition bounds the automatic consequence rather than claiming a check that does not exist.

alternatives.option: Prompt instructions only, no checks
alternatives.tradeoff: Simplest; the failure mode is a model answering a dictated question and the answer being pasted into a document.

alternatives.option: Keep a per-mode override for unpacked languages
alternatives.tradeoff: No degradation for multilingual users; lets a mode contradict its own declaration, which is the condition the specification places on answering.

alternatives.option: Skip generation entirely when no pack exists
alternatives.tradeoff: Uniform conservatism; makes pack coverage a restriction on model use, which an earlier review identified as unrelated to the requirement.

alternatives.option: Pass focused-element context as prose unconditionally
alternatives.tradeoff: Better rewrites of a draft in the field; leaves an untransformed instruction path with only after-the-fact detection.

alternatives.option: Validate with a second model asked whether the output is faithful
alternatives.tradeoff: Catches semantic drift lexical checks miss; costs a second generation pass on the latency path and inherits the same failure mode.

decisions.consequences: Modes cannot be saved without a contract, which the editor makes quick with presets. Term-list context is less useful to a model than prose, so modes that need prose opt in and accept a hold when checks are unavailable. Rewriting in a language with no pack is produced and retained but not delivered automatically for modes declaring answersQuestions false, and the panel says why with a one-click deliver. Thresholds need tuning against the fidelity corpus, and bad thresholds show up as frequent visible fallbacks.
decisions.reconsider_when: Violation and hold rates stay high on correct outputs, the adversarial corpus finds a violation class that passes every check, or term-list context proves too lossy for the modes that most need context.

decisions.title: Built-in mode set and their contracts
decisions.choice: Four read-only built-in modes, each with an explicit contract. Standard: punctuation, capitalization, optional disfluency removal, vocabulary substitution; no reordering, no summarizing, no answering. Email: Standard plus salutation and sign-off from a template, paragraph breaks, register adjustment, no new factual content, recall-bounded body. Note: adds list and heading structure, recall-bounded. Meeting notes: summarization permitted, bounded by a citation requirement where every bullet references a real segment range and uncited bullets are dropped. All four declare answersQuestions false and default every context source to term-list form. English packs ship first; other languages take the disposition in D-012.
decisions.rationale: The specification asks for ordinary dictation plus task-specific output with permitted transformations specified per mode. Meeting notes is the one mode where summarization is the point, so recall cannot be its guard and a citation requirement fits what it is allowed to do.

alternatives.option: One configurable mode with toggles
alternatives.tradeoff: Less to explain; the contract dissolves into a toggle matrix that is hard to check against.

alternatives.option: A larger built-in catalog
alternatives.tradeoff: More coverage out of the box; each mode needs its own fidelity corpus and rubric, and custom modes already cover these.

alternatives.option: Ship an assistant mode that answers dictated questions
alternatives.tradeoff: An obvious use of a local language model; it is the behavior the requirements single out as a hazard, so it would declare answersQuestions and be visibly distinct in the mode indicator.

decisions.consequences: Built-ins are read-only; customizing one duplicates it into a user mode carrying the same contract as a starting point, which keeps the built-in fidelity corpus meaningful. Four modes means four rubric corpora per shipped language, scored under the rule in verification.
decisions.reconsider_when: Users routinely duplicate a built-in to make the same edit, which is evidence the built-in should change.

decisions.title: Automatic mode selection: ordered rules, list order as the whole precedence rule, latched at arming
decisions.choice: An ordered rule list evaluated at arming, first match wins, ordered by the user. List position is the complete precedence rule; there is no priority field and no runtime specificity comparison. The editor proposes an insertion position by specificity (URL host plus path prefix, then host, then bundle identifier, then any) and flags rules that can never fire because an earlier rule shadows them. The selected mode is latched into the run manifest. A predicate whose input cannot be obtained does not match, and evaluation continues; if nothing matches, the user's default mode applies.
decisions.rationale: First match on a user-ordered list is the model people know from mail filters and makes conflict resolution inspectable by reading the list top to bottom. Specificity stays in the editor as a suggestion at authoring time, so runtime behavior never depends on a comparison the user cannot see. Treating an unobtainable predicate as a non-match keeps a missing permission from producing a wrong mode. Latching at arming means the mode cannot change under the user mid-sentence.

alternatives.option: Highest specificity wins regardless of order
alternatives.tradeoff: No shadowed rules; the user cannot temporarily override a specific rule with a general one, and precedence stops being visible.

alternatives.option: An explicit numeric priority field with specificity as tiebreak
alternatives.tradeoff: Fine-grained control; two ordering mechanisms to reconcile and a list whose display order does not determine behavior.

alternatives.option: Re-evaluate continuously during capture
alternatives.tradeoff: Follows the user across windows; the mode could change mid-sentence and the run would no longer have one manifest.

alternatives.option: Infer the mode from what was said
alternatives.tradeoff: No rules to configure; requires recognition before mode selection, inverting the pipeline.

decisions.consequences: The effective mode and whether it came from a rule or the fallback appear in the panel and menu bar for every run. Users reorder rules by dragging, which is the only precedence control. Switching applications mid-recording keeps the mode chosen where the user started. Browser URL availability is enumerated per browser instead of assumed.
decisions.reconsider_when: Rule lists grow long enough that manual ordering is unmanageable, which would argue for grouping rather than a hidden precedence rule.

decisions.title: Vocabulary as staged passes with a defined order and an explicit match precedence
decisions.choice: Four stages in fixed order. Recognition biasing puts selected terms in the decoder prompt slot, capped to the runtime limit, chosen by mode relevance and recency. Deterministic replacement scans the recognition result left to right; at each position it considers every rule matching there, takes the longest match, and breaks ties among equal-length matches by list order, applying replacements once with no cascading, boundary-aware using ICU word segmentation for the run's language, case-preserving and non-overlapping. Filler removal is a separate per-mode pass. After generation the replacement table is applied once more and vocabulary survival is checked. Recognition and normalized results are both retained. For scripts without word spacing, replacement uses ICU segmentation where available and otherwise falls back to substring matching with a warning in the vocabulary editor.
decisions.rationale: The mechanisms fail differently and must not be conflated. Prompt biasing changes decoding probabilities and guarantees nothing, so the interface says so. Deterministic replacement is exact and belongs on text. The post-generation pass exists because a language model will sometimes normalize an unusual proper noun back to a common word. Stating longest match with list order as the tie-break removes the earlier ambiguity between ordered rules and longest match, under which two implementations could produce different normalized transcripts while satisfying the prose.

alternatives.option: Pure list order, first matching rule wins
alternatives.tradeoff: Easy to explain; a short rule earlier in the list pre-empts a longer, more specific one.

alternatives.option: Replacement only after generation
alternatives.tradeoff: One pass; the generation stage then reasons over text containing mis-recognized terms.

alternatives.option: Ask the language model to apply the vocabulary
alternatives.tradeoff: Handles inflection that literal matching misses; makes an exact user-specified substitution probabilistic.

alternatives.option: Cascading replacement to a fixpoint
alternatives.tradeoff: Handles chained rules; introduces order-dependent results and possible loops.

decisions.consequences: Two texts per run to store and show. The editor must explain that terms have one probabilistic effect and one exact effect, and must show which rule won when two overlap. The prompt slot forces selection when the vocabulary is large, so the panel can show which terms were included.
decisions.reconsider_when: A runtime exposes real biasing or constrained decoding, which moves exact-name handling into recognition.

decisions.title: Context sources: sampled at arming, distilled by default, digest-only retention, stated ephemeral lifetimes
decisions.choice: Three optional sources sampled in parallel at arming against a 200 ms deadline: focused-element text, selection and window title through accessibility, capped at 4000 characters; one frame of the focused window through ScreenCaptureKit with Vision text recognition, opt-in; the first text item on the pasteboard, capped. Every source is distilled to a capped term list before it reaches the prompt unless the mode opts that source into prose, and prose carries the disposition in D-012. Anything missing the deadline is omitted and recorded as omitted. Retention defaults to digest, length, source kind and representation; retaining text is opt-in per mode and stored as an owned artifact (D-039). Transient copies have explicit release points: the screen frame dies when Vision returns and is never written to disk, source strings die once the prompt is assembled, the assembled prompt lives in the RunActor and in the service job arena until the generation completes, fails or is cancelled and is never written to disk, XPC buffers are released per credit window, and generation key-value state is freed at job end.
decisions.rationale: Sampling once at arming bounds cost and makes a run reproducible; continuous sampling would make the same recording produce different prompts depending on timing. Digest-only retention keeps the library from accumulating copies of unrelated documents and screens while letting a reprocess report that the original context is gone. Naming the release point of each transient copy, including the assembled prompt in both processes, is what makes the retention claim checkable rather than a statement about the database only.

alternatives.option: Sample at generation time
alternatives.tradeoff: Fresher context and screen recognition off the latency path; by then the user has often switched windows.

alternatives.option: Retain full context text by default
alternatives.tradeoff: Reprocessing reproduces the original result exactly; the library accumulates screen and clipboard contents by default.

alternatives.option: Continuous screen sampling during capture
alternatives.tradeoff: Captures what changed while speaking; sustained recognition cost and a much larger retention question.

decisions.consequences: Screen recognition may routinely miss the deadline on busy displays and is then absent and noted. Reprocessing a recording whose context was not retained produces a different result, and History shows why. The term-list default means context contributes vocabulary and names rather than sentences unless a mode opts in, which reduces the usefulness of context for drafting modes and is the price of removing an unchecked instruction path.
decisions.reconsider_when: Term-list context proves too lossy for the modes that most need context, which would argue for a structured intermediate representation rather than raw prose.

decisions.title: Languages: per-mode selection or detection, translation as a derived result of a named parent
decisions.choice: Each mode sets recognition language to an explicit code or to auto. Auto uses the runtime's language identification with its probability; below threshold the run records undetermined, uses the mode's default language, and the panel says so. Translation to English is a separate declared operation producing a result whose primary input names the exact recognition or normalized result it translated. Each model installation declares supported languages, labeled in the interface as declared by the publisher and unmeasured until an evaluation row exists.
decisions.rationale: Recognition quality and rewriting quality are different properties measured by different methods, so they are represented and evaluated separately. Naming the parent result is what makes translation provenance survive a second recognition of the same audio. Marking language support as declared keeps the product from promising coverage nobody measured.

alternatives.option: Always auto-detect
alternatives.tradeoff: Nothing to configure; short utterances and code-switching produce wrong detections and the user cannot pin a language they know.

alternatives.option: Translate by replacing the transcript
alternatives.tradeoff: One text per recording; the original wording is unrecoverable, breaking reprocessing and review.

alternatives.option: Translate as part of the rewrite
alternatives.tradeoff: One pass; translation and formatting become entangled and a failed check cannot separate a translation error from a formatting one.

decisions.consequences: History shows several artifacts per recording and must make the parent of each obvious. A user-supplied model with an inaccurate manifest can overstate coverage, so the interface attributes the claim to the manifest. Rewriting in a language with no pack is produced and retained but not delivered automatically for modes declaring answersQuestions false (D-012), so multilingual recognition is broader than multilingual automatic delivery and the interface states which.
decisions.reconsider_when: Measured detection accuracy on short utterances makes auto safe as the default, or a runtime provides per-segment language identification supporting code-switching.

decisions.title: One ingest port carrying timing and flow control, with a declared format matrix
decisions.choice: All sources implement AudioSource, emitting AudioFrame values that carry stream id, clock domain, presentation time, sequence number, discontinuity flag, native sample rate, channel layout and sample format. Conversion to the canonical 16 kHz mono Float32 recognition input is an explicit stage after the port. Consumers grant credit; a seekable source stops decoding when credit is exhausted, and a live source that overruns drops frames and records a discontinuity instead of buffering without bound. Credit extends across the service connection, so the window queue inside a service is bounded by the same accounting. Microphone via AVAudioEngine, system audio via ScreenCaptureKit, files via AVAssetReader in 30-second windows. Initial matrix: wav, aiff, caf, mp3, m4a in AAC and ALAC, mp4, m4v, mov. Extension: a DecoderProvider port with an opt-in external command-line decoder adapter, off by default, run inside the sandboxed decode service.
decisions.rationale: An untimestamped canonical buffer cannot express what meetings need, which is two native streams aligned by host time with drift and gaps visible, and it cannot express backpressure, which is what bounds memory end to end. Windowed decoding bounds the decoder; credit bounds the queue between decoder, converter and recognizer, including across the connection, and with the session bounds in D-004 it bounds the whole non-model footprint. RESEARCH notes whisper.cpp's example has input-format constraints, so an explicit decoding boundary is needed regardless of which runtime ships.

alternatives.option: Canonical untimestamped buffers
alternatives.tradeoff: Simplest consumer code; meeting alignment and gap reporting have to travel around the abstraction, and flow control has nowhere to live.

alternatives.option: Separate live and seekable ports
alternatives.tradeoff: Each expresses its own timing and retry rules; orchestration, cancellation and conversion get duplicated.

alternatives.option: Decode whole files into memory
alternatives.tradeoff: Simplest of all; a three-hour file at 16 kHz Float32 is roughly 700 MB before any model loads.

alternatives.option: Bundle a general-purpose decoder
alternatives.tradeoff: Every format works out of the box; adds licensing obligations, binary size and a security update duty for a decoder parsing untrusted files.

decisions.consequences: Every source carries timing metadata even when it has one stream and no drift. Live overrun is a visible discontinuity rather than a silent gap. Canonical conversion discards content above 8 kHz for recognition, so imported originals are kept and meeting streams are sealed at native rate for later use. Live overrun appears in the recording as a marked discontinuity.
decisions.reconsider_when: A speech runtime benefits from a higher input rate, or credit proves unnecessary because every runtime consumes faster than any source produces.

decisions.title: Imports are copy-in and commit-late, leaving the source untouched
decisions.choice: Import opens the source read-only, copies it into the session directory, and records a security-scoped bookmark for provenance. The recording row commits only when the artifact is complete and readable. On any failure the session directory is removed and no row exists. Moving the original happens only after commit, as a step the user can decline.
decisions.rationale: A failed import leaves its source unchanged if the import path never opens the source for writing and never deletes it. Committing after the artifact is complete keeps a failure from leaving a History entry pointing at nothing.

alternatives.option: Reference the source in place
alternatives.tradeoff: No duplication; the library breaks when the user moves or deletes the file, and reprocessing later finds nothing.

alternatives.option: Transcode on import and discard the original
alternatives.tradeoff: Smaller library and one decode path; discards information and makes reprocessing with a better decoder impossible.

alternatives.option: Create the row first and fill it in
alternatives.tradeoff: Progress visible immediately; a failure leaves a broken row for recovery to reason about.

decisions.consequences: Imports duplicate storage, visible in the library size view and covered by retention. Large video imports copy the whole file though only the audio track is used; extracting only the audio is a refinement once the cost is measured.
decisions.reconsider_when: Large video imports become common enough that storing extracted audio plus a bookmark beats keeping the original.

decisions.title: Speech runtime: WhisperKit ships, whisper.cpp is the F1 comparison harness and the designed second adapter
decisions.choice: Ship WhisperKit from the Argmax Swift package behind SpeechRecognizer, loaded inside the sandboxed speech service with an explicit local model folder and acquisition disabled. Build a measurement-only whisper.cpp harness as part of F1, not as a shipping adapter, so the retention comparison is executable. Promote it to a full adapter when Intel coverage is required, when F1 misses a range, or when the notice inventory rules the first choice out.
decisions.rationale: Three pieces of evidence in RESEARCH support choosing now instead of deferring: the runtime is distributed as a Swift package and the stated build is SPM, so integration cost is lower than a C API that also needs its own decoding boundary; the WhisperKit model repository states MIT on its card, the only positive licensing evidence available for weights the application might offer for download; and SpeakerKit ships in the same package, so the diarizer that Meetings requires arrives through one dependency. What RESEARCH does not establish is accuracy, latency or long-recording behavior. The previous revision made retention depend on a comparison with an adapter that was to be built only after retention failed, which could never be evaluated; building the comparison arm as measurement code inside F1 removes the circularity at a fraction of the cost of a second shipping adapter.

alternatives.option: whisper.cpp as the shipping runtime
alternatives.tradeoff: Intel and Apple Silicon coverage today with widely available GGML weights; C interop in the hot path, an explicit decoding boundary its example demands, and a second dependency and acquisition path for diarization.

alternatives.option: Maintain both runtimes permanently
alternatives.tradeoff: Maximum flexibility; two parameter translations, two evaluation runs per model update and two descriptor sets, paid before any evidence says both have a role.

alternatives.option: An absolute word error rate threshold instead of a comparison
alternatives.tradeoff: No second arm to build; an absolute number for a mixed-language corpus has no defensible basis and would be invented.

alternatives.option: Apple's built-in speech recognition
alternatives.tradeoff: No models to manage; on-device availability and language coverage are controlled by the system and model choice is not exposed, which the requirements demand.

decisions.consequences: F1 carries the cost of a second measurement path. Intel is unsupported until the harness is promoted. Results record the installation, runtime revision and adapter revision, so a change is visible in History. Until F1 completes, no accuracy or latency claim appears anywhere.
decisions.reconsider_when: F1 misses any of its approved ranges, the notice inventory blocks the weights the app would offer, or Intel becomes a requirement.

decisions.title: Generation runtime: llama.cpp embedded in the generation service, GGUF models
decisions.choice: Embed llama.cpp as a library in GenerationService, loading GGUF models with Metal on Apple Silicon and CPU otherwise, streaming tokens back over the connection. No server binary is used or shipped.
decisions.rationale: RESEARCH records llama.cpp as providing local inference with Metal support and as shipping both library integration material and server tooling, and asks that an embedded worker be compared with a local service including whether network access is possible. Embedding gives control over acquisition and lifecycle, and GGUF reaches the quantized models users already have, which matters because user-supplied models are in scope.

alternatives.option: MLX-based generation
alternatives.tradeoff: Apple-native with good Apple Silicon performance; a different model format, fewer ready quantizations and no Intel path.

alternatives.option: Core ML converted models
alternatives.tradeoff: System-managed execution and no vendored C++; per-model conversion work, and user-supplied models become impractical.

alternatives.option: The llama.cpp server on localhost
alternatives.tradeoff: Reuses upstream tooling; the reachability and forwarding concerns in D-003 apply directly.

decisions.consequences: Vendored C++ with build time, pinning and update discipline, and a runtime revision recorded on every run. Quantization becomes a user-visible setting with a memory consequence surfaced through D-027.
decisions.reconsider_when: MLX coverage of the quantizations users bring becomes comparable, or measured generation latency is unacceptable and another runtime measurably beats it.

decisions.title: Model identity over every behavior-affecting asset, immutable installs, transactional activation, per-kind checks, notices outside the blob
decisions.choice: Identity is publisher name, revision string and a SHA-256 over a content-addressed installation manifest listing the relative path and SHA-256 of every behavior-affecting asset: weights, tokenizer or vocabulary, model configuration, prompt or chat template, feature-extraction parameters and companions. Installation stages into Models/.staging/<uuid>, verifies per-asset and manifest hashes, runs the smoke test for its model kind in the matching service against the staged path, then renames into Models/blobs/<setHash>, a path never previously written. One SQLite transaction inserts the installation row, its per-asset rows and the active pointer; notices are written under Models/notices/<setHash>/, outside the blob directory. Every run records the runtime revision, adapter revision and capability-descriptor version. Per-kind compatibility and smoke tests: speech needs encoder, decoder and tokenizer and transcribes a three-second fixture; generation needs weights with a tokenizer and produces 16 tokens from a fixed prompt and seed; diarization needs segmenter, embedder and clusterer and returns at least one segment on a ten-second two-speaker fixture. Quality scores never gate activation. Runtimes receive absolute paths and never load by name.
decisions.rationale: A sequence spanning a filesystem rename and a database update needs an ordering rule, and renaming over a live directory is not atomic. Hashing only the weight files would let a tokenizer, template or configuration change output while History reported the same identity, and a runtime update would do the same invisibly, so identity covers every asset the runtime reads and the run pins the code revision beside it. Notices live outside the blob because archiving deletes the blob and must not delete the terms it claims to retain. A single generic smoke test cannot catch a diarizer missing its clusterer, so the descriptor and the test are per kind. RESEARCH warns that a default runtime initialization may download models, so passing explicit paths is the enforcement point, and it asks that licence and revision be preserved per selected model.

alternatives.option: Hash the weight files only
alternatives.tradeoff: Cheaper on multi-gigabyte installs; two installs identical in weights but differing in tokenizer or template are indistinguishable in History.

alternatives.option: Identity by file name or publisher identifier
alternatives.tradeoff: No hashing cost; two quantizations under one name become indistinguishable.

alternatives.option: Install in place and roll back on failure
alternatives.tradeoff: No staging space needed; a failure during the write leaves a corrupt live model.

alternatives.option: One generic load test for every model kind
alternatives.tradeoff: Less per-kind work; misses missing companion assets, which then fail mid-dictation.

alternatives.option: Let the runtime's own downloader manage models
alternatives.tradeoff: Much less code; hands acquisition to a component that may download implicitly.

decisions.consequences: Installation needs free space for the staged and stored copy, checked before starting, and hashing large files is shown as a verification step. A runtime update changes the recorded revision on new runs, so History can distinguish results the same installation produced under different code. Blobs can outlive their rows briefly after a crash and are collected at launch. Failed user imports stay in staging with the error attached.
decisions.reconsider_when: Hashing time becomes a usability problem, which argues for incremental hashing during download, or a new model kind arrives whose descriptor does not fit the per-kind pattern.

decisions.title: Meetings: SpeakerKit diarization in its own service, channel origin as fact, attribution as hypothesis
decisions.choice: Record microphone and system audio as separate artifacts with role recorded as a capture fact, aligned by host time with tone-derived drift correction, labeled as the microphone channel and the system audio channel. Diarize with SpeakerKit's Pyannote pipeline behind a Diarizer port in DiarizationService, configured with download disabled, an explicit model folder and explicit segmenter and embedder concurrency, all recorded in the manifest. Weights are user-acquired and never bundled. Diarization is a run stage with cancellation, recovery and admission (D-006, D-007, D-027) and produces an immutable diarization result plus assignment revision 1 in the same transaction. Per-segment calibrated confidence is stored as unknown and no per-segment margin is stored, because the cited declaration does not establish either. Centroid cosine distance, where a centroid exists, proposes cross-recording identity for user confirmation and never applies one. Segments correlating with delayed system audio are marked probable echo and excluded from microphone-side attribution. Notes are generated by a separate notes run over the timestamped transcript in overlapping windows with per-bullet segment citations, and uncited bullets are dropped.
decisions.rationale: The requirement asks for speaker assignment, editable names and an explicit runtime choice, so the runtime is named: it lives in the package already selected for speech, and RESEARCH documents the configuration flags that keep it from downloading, which is also why it gets its own sandboxed service. RESEARCH establishes that v1.1.0 exposes centroid embeddings with cosine-distance helpers, that a speaker may lack a centroid, and that the declaration does not establish per-segment confidence or margin; the schema follows that boundary rather than assuming richer evidence. A microphone can pick up remote audio from speakers and a system stream can carry several applications, so channel origin is not identity. Cluster numbers are arbitrary across runs, so names live on identities and assignment revisions (D-037).

alternatives.option: Diarize a single mixed recording
alternatives.tradeoff: One file and one capture path; discards the channel signal and makes even the easiest question an inference.

alternatives.option: Treat channels as speaker identity
alternatives.tradeoff: Labels users understand immediately; wrong whenever speakers leak into the microphone or several people share a room.

alternatives.option: Store a per-segment margin derived from clustering internals
alternatives.tradeoff: Would give a per-segment quality signal; the cited declaration exposes none, so it would be an invented number.

alternatives.option: Apply cross-recording identity automatically above a distance threshold
alternatives.tradeoff: Less user work across a meeting series; the SDK defines no universal threshold.
